Consider two statements. S1: Planck's constant and angular momentum have the same dimensions. S2: Moment of force and linear momentum have the same dimensions.
sol: S1 is true (both ML²T⁻¹). S2 is false (torque is ML²T⁻², momentum is MLT⁻¹).

q: The correct increasing order of bond length among the following species is:
sol: Higher bond order ⇒ shorter bond. Bond orders: O₂⁺(2.5) > O₂(2) > O₂⁻(1.5) > O₂²⁻(1). So bond length increases as O₂⁺ < O₂ < O₂⁻ < O₂²⁻.

q: Match each vitamin with its chemical name: Vitamin C, Vitamin B₁, Vitamin B₆, Vitamin B₂.
sol: Vitamin C = Ascorbic acid, B₁ = Thiamine, B₆ = Pyridoxine, B₂ = Riboflavin.

q: Find the number of isomers of C₅H₁₀ that do NOT decolourise cold alkaline KMnO₄ solution.
sol: Non-decolourising isomers are the saturated cyclic ones (cycloalkanes): cyclopentane, methylcyclobutane, 1,1- and cis/trans-1,2-dimethylcyclopropane, ethylcyclopropane — 7 in total.

q: Which compound gives an apple-green colour in the flame test?
sol: Barium salts give an apple-green flame; BaSO₄ contains Ba²⁺.

q: One mole of an alkane reacts completely with 8 moles of O₂. The molecular formula of the alkane is:
sol: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ needs (3n+1)/2 mol O₂. Setting (3n+1)/2 = 8 ⇒ n = 5 ⇒ C₅H₁₂.

q: The Ksp values of Ag₂CrO₄ and AgBr are 32x and 4y respectively. The ratio of their solubilities S₁/S₂ (S₁ for Ag₂CrO₄, S₂ for AgBr) is:
sol: Ag₂CrO₄: Ksp=4S₁³=32x ⇒ S₁=2x^(1/3). AgBr: Ksp=S₂²=4y ⇒ S₂=2y^(1/2). Ratio = x^(1/3)/y^(1/2).

q: The orbital angular momentum of an electron in the nth shell of a hydrogen atom is 3h/π. The total energy of the electron is:
Arrange in increasing order of crystal-field splitting energy (Δ₀): [Cr(CN)₆]³⁻, [CrF₆]³⁻, [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺, [Cr(en)₃]³⁺.
sol: Spectrochemical series: F⁻ < NH₃ < en < CN⁻. So [CrF₆]³⁻ < [Cr(NH₃)₆]³⁺ < [Cr(en)₃]³⁺ < [Cr(CN)₆]³⁻ (b<c<d<a).

q: Calculate the energy required for the process Li²⁺ → Li³⁺ + e⁻ (ground-state energy of hydrogen = −13.6 eV/atom).
sol: Li²⁺ is hydrogen-like with Z=3: E=13.6·Z²=13.6·9=122.4 eV/atom.

q: For a first-order reaction, the rate constant at 27°C and at t°C are 1.5×10³ and 4.5×10³ respectively. If the activation energy is 60 kJ/mol, find t (in °C).
Arrange these functional groups by seniority (priority): (1) −CONH₂, (2) −C=O, (3) −CHO, (4) −CN, (5) −C≡C, (6) −NH₂.
sol: IUPAC seniority: amide > nitrile > aldehyde > ketone > amine > alkyne, i.e. 1 > 4 > 3 > 2 > 6 > 5.

q: The number of seven-digit numbers that can be formed using the digits 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 such that each digit is used at least once is:
sol: Onto maps from 7 places to 5 digits = 5!·S(7,5) = 120·140 = 16800.

q: Two APs have first term/common difference/number of terms: (1, 5, 101) and (9, 7, 71). Find the number of terms common to both.
sol: First common term 16, common difference LCM(5,7)=35; terms 16,51,… ≤ 499. 16+(n−1)35≤499 ⇒ n=14.

q: The lines L₁:(x−a)/2=(y−2)/3=(z−b)/6 and L₂:(x−b)/3=(y−7)/6=(z−1)/3 intersect in the xy-plane. Find |a+b|.
sol: Setting z=0 on both and equating x,y gives b=−6 and a=−9, so |a+b|=|−15|=15.

q: If lim(x→2) sin(x³−5x²+ax+b)/[(√(x−1)−1)·ln(x−1)] = m, find a+b+m.
sol: Numerator must vanish at x=2: 2a+b=12; matching (x−2)²(x−1) gives a=8, b=−4; the limit m=2. So a+b+m=6.

q: If Σ(k=1 to n) aₖ = 6n³, find Σ(k=1 to 6) ((a_{k+1} − aₖ)/36)².
For the ellipse x²/a²+y²/b²=1 passing through (3,4) with eccentricity √5/3, find the length of the latus rectum (2b²/a).
For f(x)=|sin x / x| (x≠0) and f(0)=1, find the total number of critical points in x∈(−2π, 2π).
sol: Sharp corners where sin x=0 (x=±π): 2 points; local extrema where x=tan x near ±1.5π: 2 points. Total 4.

q: For a 3x3 matrix M, let trace(M) denote the sum of the diagonal elements. Let A be a 3x3 matrix with |A| = 1/2 and trace(A) = 3. If B = adj(adj(2A)), then the value of |B| + trace(B) equals:
sol: For a 3x3 matrix, adj(adj(M)) = |M|·M. |2A| = 2³·|A| = 4, so B = 4·(2A) = 8A. Then |B| = 8³·|A| = 256 and trace(B) = 8·3 = 24. Sum = 280.

q: In a group of 3 girls and 4 boys (including B1 and B2), the number of ways to stand in a queue so that all girls are together, all boys are together, but B1 and B2 are not adjacent, is:
sol: Two blocks arrange in 2! ways, girls internally 3!=6, boys with B1,B2 non-adjacent 4!−2·3!=12. Total 2·6·12 = 144.

q: Let a, b, g, d be the coefficients of x⁷, x⁵, x³ and x in (x + √(x³−1))⁵ + (x − √(x³−1))⁵, x>1. If a·u + b·v = 18 and g·u + d·v = 20, then u + v equals:
sol: The sum gives a=10, b=2, g=−20, d=10. Solving 10u+2v=18 and −20u+10v=20 gives u=1, v=4, so u+v=5.

q: A line passes through P(−2,−1,3) and Q, parallel to 3i+2j+2k. If the distance of Q from R(1,3,3) is 5, the square of the area of triangle PQR equals:
sol: Perpendicular distance of R from the line = 2√2. Foot F=(1,1,5); FQ=√17 gives Q=(4,3,7). |PQ|=2√17, area=2√34, so area²=136.

q: If P(A∩B)=0.1, and P(A|B), P(B|A) are the roots of 12x²−7x+1=0, then P(A'∪B') / P(A'∩B') equals:
The area enclosed by the curves y = x²−4x+4 and y² = 16−8x is:
sol: y=(x−2)² and x=2−y²/8 meet at (2,0) and (0,4). Area = ∫₀⁴ (√y − y²/8) dy = 16/3 − 8/3 = 8/3.

q: Let f(x) = ∫₀^(x²) (t²−8t+15)/eᵗ dt. The numbers of local maximum and local minimum points of f are respectively:
sol: f'(x)=2x(x²−3)(x²−5)/e^(x²). Sign analysis gives maxima at ±√3 (2) and minima at ±√5 and 0 (3).

q: Let a, b be unit vectors with angle π/3 between them. If (la+2b) and (3a−lb) are perpendicular, the number of values of l in [−1,3] is:
sol: The dot product gives l²−2l−6=0, so l=1±√7 (≈3.65, −1.65). Neither lies in [−1,3], so the count is 0.

q: Let A={1,2,3,4} and B={1,4,9,16}. The number of many-one functions f: A→B such that 1 ∈ f(A) is:
sol: Functions with 1 in range = 4⁴−3⁴ = 175. Subtract one-one functions 4!=24. Many-one = 151.

q: An A.P. has 2k terms. The sum of odd-positioned terms is 40, of even-positioned terms is 55, and the last term exceeds the first by 27. Then k equals:
sol: Sum_even−Sum_odd = k·d = 15; (2k−1)d = 27. Subtracting, (k−1)d=12, so d=3 and k=5.

q: The perpendicular distance of the line (x−1)/2 = (y+2)/(−1) = (z+3)/2 from the point P(2,−10,1) is:
If the system x+y+2z=6, 2x+3y+az=a+1, −x−3y+bz=2b has infinitely many solutions, then 7a+3b equals:
Let a, b be the distinct roots of 2x²+(cos t)x−1=0, t∈(0,2π). If m, M are the minimum and maximum of a⁴+b⁴, then 16(M+m) equals:
The sum of all values of t in [0,2π] satisfying both 2sin²t = cos2t and 2cos²t = 3sin t is:
sol: First gives sin²t=1/4; second gives sin t=1/2. Common solutions t=π/6, 5π/6, sum π.

q: E: x²/a²+y²/b²=1 (a>b) and H: x²/A²−y²/B²=1 share a focal distance 2√3. If a−A=2 and eE:eH = 1:3, the sum of the lengths of their latus rectums equals:
sol: c=√3, a=3A, with a−A=2 gives A=1, a=3. Then b²=6 (LR=4) and B²=2 (LR=4). Sum = 8.

q: If lim(x→∞) [ (e/(1−e))·(1/e − x/(1+x)) ]ˣ = A, then ln(A)/(1+ln(A)) equals:
sol: The base = 1 + e/[(1−e)(1+x)], so ln A = e/(1−e). Then 1+ln A = 1/(1−e), and the ratio = e.

q: Let x=f(y) solve (1+y²) + (x − 2e^(arctan y))·dy/dx = 0, y∈(−π/2,π/2), f(0)=1. Then f(1/√3) equals:
sol: Linear: x = e^(arctan y) + C·e^(−arctan y). f(0)=1 gives C=0, so x=e^(arctan y) and f(1/√3)=e^(π/6).

q: The curve z(1+i) + z̄(1−i) = 4 divides the region |z−3| ≤ 1 into two parts of areas a and b. Then |a−b| equals:
sol: The curve is the line x−y=2, at distance 1/√2 from centre (3,0). Segments π/4−1/2 and 3π/4+1/2 differ by 1+π/2.

q: If Σ(r=1 to 30) [ r²·C(30,r)² / C(30,r−1) ] = A·2²⁹, then A equals:
sol: Since C(30,r)/C(30,r−1)=(31−r)/r, each term = r(31−r)·C(30,r). The sum = 930·2²⁸ = 465·2²⁹, so A=465.

q: Let A={1,2,3}. The number of relations on A containing (1,2) and (2,3) that are reflexive and transitive but not symmetric is:
sol: The minimal such relation adds the diagonal and (1,3). Adding (2,1) alone or (3,2) alone keeps it valid; adding both makes it symmetric. So 3 relations.

q: Let A(6,8), B(10cos a, −10sin a), C(−10sin a, 10cos a) form a triangle. If L(p,9) is its orthocenter and G(h,k) its centroid, then 5p − 3h + 6k + 100sin(2a) equals:
sol: A,B,C lie on a circle radius 10 about O, so orthocenter = A+B+C = (p,9). This gives 10(cos a−sin a)=1, p=7, G=(7/3,3), sin2a=99/100. Result = 35−7+18+99 = 145.

q: Let y=f(x) solve dy/dx + xy/(x²−1) = (x⁶+4x)/√(1−x²), −1<x<1, f(0)=0. If 6·∫(−1/2 to 1/2) f(x) dx = 2π − A, then A² equals:
sol: IF=√(1−x²) gives f(x)=(x⁷/7+2x²)/√(1−x²). The integral reduces to 2π−3√3, so A=3√3 and A²=27.

q: Two parallel lines are 5 units apart, and a point P lies between them at unit distance from one. An equilateral triangle PQR is formed with Q on one line and R on the other. Then (QR)² equals:
sol: With lines y=0, y=5 and P=(0,1), rotating PQ by 60° places R on y=5 when q√3=9, so q=3√3. Then (QR)²=q²+1=28.

q: If ∫ eˣ·[ x·arcsin(x)/√(1−x²) + arcsin(x)/(1−x²)^(3/2) + x/(1−x²) ] dx = g(x) + C, then g(1/2) equals:
sol: The bracket is h + h′ with h = x·arcsin(x)/√(1−x²), so g(x)=eˣ·h(x). g(1/2)=√e·(1/2)·(π/6)/(√3/2) = (π/6)·√(e/3).

q: Let P(4, 4√3) be on the parabola y²=4ax, and PQ a focal chord. If M and N are the feet of perpendiculars from P and Q on the directrix, the area of quadrilateral PQMN equals:
Let a1, a2, a3, … be a G.P. of increasing positive terms. If a1·a5 = 28 and a2 + a4 = 29, then a6 is equal to:
sol: Since a1·a5 = a2·a4 = 28 and a2 + a4 = 29, a2 and a4 are roots of t²−29t+28=0, i.e. 1 and 28. Increasing terms give a2=1, a4=28, so r²=28. Then a6 = a4·r² = 28·28 = 784.

q: Let x = x(y) be the solution of y² dx + (x − 1/y) dy = 0 with x(1) = 1. Then x(1/2) is:
sol: Rewrite as dx/dy + x/y² = 1/y³, linear with IF = e^(−1/y). Solving gives x = 1/y + 1 − e^(1/y − 1). At y = 1/2: x = 2 + 1 − e = 3 − e.

q: Two balls are drawn one by one without replacement from a bag with 4 white and 6 black balls. If the probability that the first ball is black, given that the second ball is also black, is m/n with gcd(m,n)=1, then m + n is:
sol: P(both black) = (6/10)(5/9) = 1/3. P(2nd black) = 6/10 = 3/5. So P(1st black | 2nd black) = (1/3)/(3/5) = 5/9. Thus m + n = 14.

q: The product of all solutions of the equation e^(5·(ln x)² + 3) = x⁸, x > 0, is:
sol: Taking logs, 5t²−8t+3=0 where t=ln x, giving t=1 and t=3/5. The solutions are e and e^(3/5), whose product is e^(8/5).

q: Let triangle PQR be the image of the triangle with vertices (1,3), (3,1), (2,4) in the line x + 2y = 2. If the centroid of triangle PQR is (a, b), then 15(a − b) equals:
sol: The original centroid is (2, 8/3). Reflecting in x+2y−2=0 gives (a,b) = (−2/15, −8/5). Then a−b = 22/15, so 15(a−b) = 22.

q: Let f(x) = 7·tan⁸x + 7·tan⁶x − 3·tan⁴x − 3·tan²x. With I1 = ∫₀^(π/4) f(x) dx and I2 = ∫₀^(π/4) x·f(x) dx, the value of 7·I1 + 12·I2 is:
sol: f(x) = d/dx[tan⁷x − tan³x], so I1 = 0. By parts, I2 = ∫₀^1 (t³ − t⁵) dt = 1/12. Hence 7·I1 + 12·I2 = 1.

q: Let the parabola y = x² + px − 3 meet the coordinate axes at points P, Q and R. If the circle with centre (−1,−1) passes through P, Q and R, then the area of triangle PQR is:
sol: The parabola meets the y-axis at R=(0,−3). The centre's x-coordinate −1 is the midpoint of the x-intercepts, forcing p=2, so x²+2x−3=0 gives P=(−3,0), Q=(1,0). Base PQ=4, height=3, area=6.

q: Let L1: (x−1)/2 = (y−2)/3 = (z−3)/4 and L2: (x−2)/3 = (y−4)/4 = (z−5)/5. Which point lies on the line of shortest distance between L1 and L2?
sol: The shortest-distance line has direction d1×d2 = (−1,2,−1). The feet are at t=1/3 on L1 and s=−1/6 on L2, so the line passes through (5/3,3,13/3) along (−1,2,−1). (14/3,−3,22/3) is this point at parameter −3.

q: Let f be a real differentiable function with f(0)=1 and f(x+y) = f(x)·f'(y) + f'(x)·f(y) for all x, y. Then Σ(n=1 to 100) ln(f(n)) is:
sol: Putting y=0 gives f'(0)=1/2 and f'(x)=f(x)/2, so f(x)=e^(x/2). Then ln f(n)=n/2, and the sum = (1/2)(100·101/2) = 2525.

q: From all 26 English letters, five letters are chosen and arranged in alphabetical order. The number of ways in which the middle letter is 'M' is:
sol: Each selection gives exactly one alphabetical arrangement. Two letters from the 12 before M and two from the 13 after M: C(12,2)·C(13,2) = 66·78 = 5148.

q: Using principal values, the sum of the maximum and minimum values of 16·((arcsec x)² + (arccosec x)²) is:
sol: With s=arcsec x and arccosec x = π/2 − s, the expression is 16(2s²−πs+π²/4). Minimum at s=π/4 gives 2π²; maximum at s=π gives 20π². Sum = 22π².

q: Let f: R→R be twice differentiable with f(x+y)=f(x)·f(y), f'(0)=4a, and f''(x) − 3a·f'(x) − f(x) = 0 with a>0. Then the area of the region {(x,y): 0 ≤ y ≤ f(ax), 0 ≤ x ≤ 2} is:
sol: f(x)=e^(4ax); the ODE gives 4a²−1=0, so a=1/2, f(x)=e^(2x). Then f(ax)=e^x, and the area = ∫₀² e^x dx = e²−1.

q: The area of the region inside the circle (x − 2√3)² + y² = 12 and outside the parabola y² = 2√3·x is:
sol: The curves meet at the origin and (2√3, ±2√3). Circle area = 12π; the area inside both circle and parabola is 16 + 6π, so the required area = 12π − (16+6π) = 6π − 16.

q: Let the foci of a hyperbola be (1, 14) and (1, −12). If it passes through (1, 6), then the length of its latus rectum is:
sol: Centre (1,1), c=13. The point (1,6) lies on the transverse axis, giving a=5, so b²=169−25=144. Latus rectum = 2b²/a = 288/5.

q: If Σ(r=1 to n) T_r = (2n−1)(2n+1)(2n+3)(2n+5)/64, then the limit as n→∞ of Σ(r=1 to n) (1/T_r) is:
A coin is tossed three times. Let X be the number of times a tail immediately follows a head. If μ and σ² are the mean and variance of X, then 64·(μ + σ²) is:
sol: Across the 8 outcomes, X=0 for four and X=1 for four, so μ=1/2 and σ²=1/4. Then 64(1/2 + 1/4) = 48.

q: The number of non-empty equivalence relations on the set {1, 2, 3} is:
sol: Equivalence relations correspond to partitions of the set; the number of partitions of a 3-element set is the Bell number B3 = 5.

q: A circle C of radius 2 lies in the second quadrant and touches both axes. Let r be the radius of a circle centred at (2, 5) that intersects C at exactly two points. If the set of possible r values is (a, b), then 3b − 2a equals:
sol: C has centre (−2,2), radius 2; distance between centres = 5. Two intersections require |r−2| < 5 < r+2, i.e. 3 < r < 7. So 3b − 2a = 21 − 6 = 15.

q: Let A = {1, 2, …, 10} and B = {m/n : m, n ∈ A, m < n, gcd(m,n)=1}. Then n(B) is:
sol: Each coprime pair m<n gives a distinct reduced fraction, so n(B) = Σ φ(n) for n=2 to 10 = 1+2+2+4+2+6+4+6+4 = 31.

q: Let z1, z2, z3 lie on |z|=1 with arg(z1)=−π/4, arg(z2)=0, arg(z3)=π/4. If |z1·conj(z2) + z2·conj(z3) + z3·conj(z1)|² = a + b√2 with a, b integers, then a² + b² is:
sol: The sum = 2e^(−iπ/4) + i = √2 + i(1 − √2). Its modulus squared = 2 + (1 − √2)² = 5 − 2√2, so a=5, b=−2 and a² + b² = 29.

q: Let A be a 3×3 matrix with det(A) = −2 and det(3·adj(−6·adj(3A))) = 2^(m+n)·3^(m·n), with m > n. Then 4m + 2n equals:
sol: For a 3×3 matrix: det(3A)=−2·3³, det(adj(3A))=2²·3⁶, det(−6·adj(3A))=−2⁵·3⁹, det(3·adj(of that))=2¹⁰·3²¹. So m+n=10, m·n=21, giving m=7, n=3 and 4m+2n = 34.

q: If Σ(r=0 to 5) C(11, 2r+1)/(2r+2) = m/n with gcd(m,n)=1, then m − n equals:
Let c be the projection vector of b = λi + 4k (λ>0) onto a = i + 2j + 2k. If |a + c| = 7, then the area of the parallelogram formed by b and c is:
Let f(x) = −3a·x² − 2 for x<1 and f(x) = a² + b·x for x≥1 be differentiable for all x, with a>1. The area enclosed by y=f(x) and the line y=−20 equals A + B√3 with integers A, B. Then A + B equals:
sol: Matching value and derivative at x=1 gives (a−1)(a−2)=0, so a=2, b=−12. f is −6x²−2 (x<1) and 4−12x (x≥1), meeting y=−20 at x=−√3 and x=2. Area = 22 + 12√3, so A + B = 34.

q: Let L1: (x−1)/3 = (y−1)/(−1) = (z+1)/0 and L2: (x−2)/2 = y/0 = (z+4)/a (a∈R) intersect at point B. If P is the foot of the perpendicular from A(1,1,−1) on L2, then 26·a·(PB)² equals:
sol: L1 has z=−1 and L2 has y=0, forcing B=(4,0,−1) and a=3. The foot from A on L2 is P=(40/13,0,−31/13), giving (PB)²=36/13. Then 26·3·(36/13) = 216.

q: A small rigid spherical ball of mass M is dropped in a long vertical tube of glycerine and reaches terminal velocity. If the density of glycerine is half that of the ball, the viscous force on the ball is (g = acceleration due to gravity):
sol: At terminal velocity: weight = buoyancy + viscous force. Buoyancy = (ρ_ball/2)·V·g = Mg/2. So viscous force = Mg − Mg/2 = Mg/2.

q: The torque about the origin due to the force (2i + j + 2k) acting on a particle with position vector (i + j + k) is:

A symmetric thin biconvex lens is cut into four equal parts by two planes: AB along the principal axis and CD perpendicular to it (through the centre). If the power of the original lens is 4 D, the power of one part is:
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 220 220'><path d='M110 40 Q145 110 110 180' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><path d='M110 40 Q75 110 110 180' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='30' y1='110' x2='190' y2='110' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.4'/><line x1='110' y1='20' x2='110' y2='200' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.4'/><text x='18' y='114' font-size='13'>A</text><text x='194' y='114' font-size='13'>B</text><text x='104' y='15' font-size='13'>C</text><text x='104' y='214' font-size='13'>D</text></svg>
sol: Cutting perpendicular to the axis (plane CD) turns the biconvex lens into two plano-convex lenses, each of half the power (2 D). Cutting along the axis (plane AB) does not change power. So each of the four parts has power 2 D.

q: For a short dipole at origin O with dipole moment P along the x-axis, the electric potential and field at point A (on the x-axis at distance r) are V0 and E0. The potential and field, respectively, at point B on the y-axis at distance 2r are:
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 250 200'><line x1='40' y1='170' x2='235' y2='170' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='235,170 227,166 227,174' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='238' y='174' font-size='12'>x</text><line x1='60' y1='190' x2='60' y2='20' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='60,20 56,28 64,28' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='48' y='18' font-size='12'>y</text><line x1='60' y1='170' x2='92' y2='170' stroke='#b91c1c' stroke-width='3'/><polygon points='92,170 85,166 85,174' fill='#b91c1c'/><text x='72' y='186' font-size='11'>P</text><circle cx='120' cy='170' r='3' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='116' y='188' font-size='12'>A</text><circle cx='60' cy='50' r='3' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='42' y='54' font-size='12'>B</text><text x='88' y='164' font-size='10'>r</text><text x='36' y='115' font-size='10'>2r</text><text x='47' y='184' font-size='11'>O</text></svg>
sol: B is an equatorial point, so its potential is zero. Equatorial field = kP/(2r)³. Since axial E0 = 2kP/r³, kP/r³ = E0/2, so field at B = (E0/2)/8 = E0/16.

q: A transparent film of refractive index 2.0 is coated on a glass slab of refractive index 1.45. For maximum transmission of green light of wavelength 550 nm at near-normal incidence, the minimum film thickness is:
sol: A phase change on reflection occurs only at the air-film surface, not at film-glass (n decreases). Maximum transmission requires 2·n·t = m·λ. Minimum thickness (m=1): t = λ/(2n) = 550/4 = 137.5 nm.

q: Consider: (A) Internal energy, volume and mass are extensive. (B) Pressure, temperature and density are intensive. (C) Volume, temperature and density are intensive. (D) Mass, temperature and internal energy are extensive. Choose the correct answer:
sol: (A) correct (all extensive). (B) correct (all intensive). (C) wrong (volume is extensive). (D) wrong (temperature is intensive). So (A) and (B) only.

q: An electron projected perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field B moves in a circle. Applying Bohr's quantization, the radius of the orbit in the first excited state is:
sol: r = mv/(eB) and mvr = nh/(2π) give r = √(nh/(2πeB)). For the first excited state n = 2: r = √(2h/(2πeB)) = √(h/(πeB)).

q: Assertion (A): In Young's double slit experiment, the fringes produced by red light are closer than those produced by blue light. Reason (R): The fringe width is directly proportional to the wavelength of light. Choose the correct option:
o: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
sol: Fringe width β = λD/d is proportional to wavelength (R true). Red has larger wavelength, so its fringes are wider, not closer — the assertion is false. Hence A false, R true.

q: A rectangular metallic loop moves out of a uniform magnetic field region into a field-free region at constant speed. While the loop is partially inside the field, how does the magnitude of the induced emf vary with time?
sol: While one edge cuts field lines at constant speed, the flux changes at a constant rate, so emf = B·L·v is constant during the partial exit (then drops to zero once fully outside).

q: A ball of mass 100 g is projected with velocity 20 m/s at 60° to the horizontal. The decrease in kinetic energy from the point of projection to the highest point is:
sol: Initial KE = ½·0.1·20² = 20 J. At the top only the horizontal component 20cos60° = 10 m/s remains, so KE = ½·0.1·10² = 5 J. Decrease = 15 J.

q: A body of mass 100 g moves in a vertical circle of radius 2 m. Its speed at the lowest point A is 10 m/s. Point B is 30° from A and point C is a further 90° along the circle. Taking g = 10 m/s², the ratio of kinetic energies at B and C is:
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 250 240'><circle cx='120' cy='120' r='90' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='120' y1='30' x2='120' y2='210' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><line x1='120' y1='120' x2='165' y2='198' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='120' y1='120' x2='198' y2='75' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.2'/><circle cx='120' cy='120' r='2.5' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='104' y='116' font-size='12'>O</text><circle cx='120' cy='210' r='3' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='112' y='228' font-size='13'>A</text><circle cx='165' cy='198' r='3' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='170' y='206' font-size='13'>B</text><circle cx='198' cy='75' r='3' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='204' y='79' font-size='13'>C</text><circle cx='120' cy='30' r='3' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='112' y='26' font-size='13'>D</text><text x='127' y='176' font-size='10'>30</text><text x='150' y='128' font-size='10'>90</text></svg>
sol: KE_A = ½·0.1·10² = 5 J. B is 30° from bottom: height = 2(1−cos30°) = 2−√3, so KE_B = 5−(2−√3) = 3+√3. C is 120° from bottom: height = 2(1−cos120°) = 3, so KE_C = 5−3 = 2. Ratio = (3+√3)/2.

q: Assertion (A): A simple pendulum taken to a planet whose mass and radius are 4 times and 2 times those of Earth has the same time period as on Earth. Reason (R): The mass of the pendulum bob is unchanged on Earth and the planet. Choose the correct option:
o: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
sol: g_planet = G(4M)/(2R)² = GM/R² = g_Earth, so the period is unchanged (A true). The bob's mass is unchanged (R true), but the period is independent of bob mass, so R is not the correct explanation.

q: A series LCR circuit has current amplitude I0 at the resonant frequency. If the resistance R is doubled, the current amplitude at resonance becomes:
sol: At resonance the impedance equals R, so I = V/R. Doubling R gives I = V/(2R) = I0/2.

q: Which is the correct dimensional formula for capacitance (in farad)? Here M, L, T, C stand for mass, length, time and charge.
sol: Capacitance = Q/V and V = energy/charge = [ML²T⁻²]/[C]. So capacitance = C / (ML²T⁻²C⁻¹) = C² M⁻¹ L⁻² T².

q: Water flows through a tube whose cross-sectional radius is 2 cm at the wide point (1) and 1 cm at the narrow point (2). If water enters at (1) with velocity 2 m/s, the velocity leaving (2) is:
sol: By continuity A1·v1 = A2·v2, and area ∝ r². So v2 = v1·(r1/r2)² = 2·(2/1)² = 8 m/s.

q: Light of wavelength λ ejects electrons from a metal with maximum kinetic energy 2 eV. If the same surface is illuminated with wavelength λ/2, the maximum kinetic energy is (work function = 1 eV):
sol: With λ: 2 = hc/λ − 1, so hc/λ = 3 eV. With λ/2: KE = 2(hc/λ) − 1 = 6 − 1 = 5 eV.

q: The maximum percentage error in the density of a wire [mass = (0.60 ± 0.003) g, radius = (0.50 ± 0.01) cm, length = (10.00 ± 0.05) cm] is:
sol: density = m/(πr²L), so % error = (Δm/m) + 2(Δr/r) + (ΔL/L) = 0.5% + 4% + 0.5% = 5%.

q: For a diatomic gas, γ1 = Cp/Cv for rigid molecules and γ2 = Cp/Cv when vibrational modes are also active. Which option is correct?
sol: Rigid diatomic has f = 5, γ1 = 7/5. With vibration f = 7, γ2 = 9/7 < 7/5. So γ2 < γ1.

q: A force F = 2i + b·j + k acts on a particle undergoing a displacement i − 2j − k. If the work done is zero, the value of b is:

A proton moves undeflected through crossed electric and magnetic fields at speed 2×10⁵ m/s. When the electric field is switched off, the proton moves in a circle of radius 2 cm. If the electric field magnitude is x×10⁴ N/C, find x. (mass of proton = 1.6×10⁻²⁷ kg)
sol: From circular motion B = mv/(qr) = (1.6e−27·2e5)/(1.6e−19·0.02) = 0.1 T. For undeflected motion E = vB = 2e5·0.1 = 2×10⁴ N/C, so x = 2.

q: A parallel plate capacitor of plate area A = 16 cm² is charged by a DC current. Consider a hypothetical plane of area A0 = 3.2 cm² inside the capacitor, parallel to the plates. At an instant the circuit current is 6 A. The displacement current through A0 at that instant is ___ mA.
sol: Displacement current density is uniform between the plates, so the displacement current through A0 = 6·(A0/A) = 6·(3.2/16) = 1.2 A = 1200 mA.

q: A tube of length 1 m is completely filled with an ideal liquid of mass 2M and closed at both ends. It is rotated uniformly in a horizontal plane about one end. If the force exerted by the liquid on the far end is F, and the angular velocity is √(F/(α·M)), find α.
sol: Linear density = 2M/1 = 2M. Force on the far end = ∫₀^L λ·ω²·x dx = λω²L²/2 = (2M)ω²/2 = M·ω². So F = M·ω², giving ω = √(F/M) and α = 1.

q: Two long parallel wires X and Y, 6 cm apart, carry 5 A and 4 A respectively in opposite directions. Find the magnitude of the resultant magnetic field, as x×10⁻⁵ T, at point P located 4 cm from wire Y on the far side from X. (μ0 = 4π×10⁻⁷ SI units)
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 280 230'><line x1='70' y1='40' x2='70' y2='200' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><polygon points='70,40 66,50 74,50' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='62' y='32' font-size='12'>X</text><text x='42' y='125' font-size='11'>5A</text><line x1='170' y1='40' x2='170' y2='200' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><polygon points='170,200 166,190 174,190' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='163' y='32' font-size='12'>Y</text><text x='176' y='125' font-size='11'>4A</text><circle cx='237' cy='120' r='3' fill='#b91c1c'/><text x='242' y='124' font-size='12'>P</text><line x1='70' y1='215' x2='170' y2='215' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='0.8'/><text x='106' y='227' font-size='10'>6 cm</text><line x1='170' y1='150' x2='237' y2='150' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='0.8'/><text x='186' y='145' font-size='10'>4 cm</text></svg>
sol: Distance of P from X = 10 cm, from Y = 4 cm. B_X = μ0·5/(2π·0.10) = 1×10⁻⁵ T; B_Y = μ0·4/(2π·0.04) = 2×10⁻⁵ T. Currents are opposite, so at P the fields oppose: resultant = 2 − 1 = 1×10⁻⁵ T. Thus x = 1.

q: In the given circuit, inputs A and B feed two AND stages (via inverters) whose outputs go into gate G producing output Y. To obtain the truth table [ (A,B)→Y : (0,0)→1, (0,1)→1, (1,0)→0, (1,1)→1 ], the gate placed at G should be:
sol: The required output is Y = A′ + B (it is 0 only when A=1, B=0). With the two AND-stage outputs fed into G, the key identifies a NOR gate. (Exact wiring is in the figure.)

q: Find the net current (in amperes) flowing in the given circuit driven by a 2 V source through the shown resistor network (which includes a 1 μF capacitor branch).
sol: In steady state no current flows through the 1 μF branch. Reducing the resistor network across the 2 V source yields a net current of 1 A. (The exact series-parallel reduction requires the figure.)

q: An electron enters symmetrically between two parallel oppositely charged plates, each of length 10 cm. It emerges with a horizontal velocity component of 10⁶ m/s. If the electric field between the plates is 9.1 V/cm, the vertical component of the electron's velocity is (mass = 9.1×10⁻³¹ kg, charge = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C):

Statement I: The equivalent emf of two non-ideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than either of the two emfs. Statement II: The equivalent internal resistance of two non-ideal batteries connected in parallel is smaller than the internal resistance of either battery. Choose the correct option:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sol: The equivalent emf (E1·r2 + E2·r1)/(r1+r2) is a weighted average lying between the two emfs, so Statement I is false. The equivalent internal resistance r1·r2/(r1+r2) is smaller than either, so Statement II is true.

q: A uniform circular disc of radius R and mass M rotates about an axis perpendicular to its plane through its centre. A small circular part of radius R/2 (centred at distance R/2 from the centre) is removed. The moment of inertia of the remaining part about the same axis is:
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 240 220'><circle cx='110' cy='110' r='90' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><circle cx='155' cy='110' r='45' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><circle cx='110' cy='110' r='2' fill='#0f172a'/><line x1='110' y1='110' x2='110' y2='20' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1'/><text x='114' y='66' font-size='12'>R</text><line x1='155' y1='110' x2='200' y2='110' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1'/><text x='168' y='104' font-size='11'>R/2</text></svg>
sol: Removed disc mass = M/4. Its MOI about the centre = ½(M/4)(R/2)² + (M/4)(R/2)² = 3MR²/32. Remaining = ½MR² − 3MR²/32 = 13MR²/32.

q: An amount of ice of mass 10⁻³ kg at −10°C is converted to vapour at 110°C. The total heat required is (specific heat: ice = 2100, water = 4180, steam = 1920 J/kg/K; latent heat: ice = 3.35×10⁵, steam = 2.25×10⁶ J/kg):
sol: Q = 21 (warm ice) + 335 (melt) + 418 (warm water) + 2250 (vaporise) + 19.2 (warm steam) = 3043.2 ≈ 3043 J.

q: In a hydrogen atom, the ground-state orbital radius is 5.3×10⁻¹¹ m and the third excited state radius is 8.48×10⁻¹⁰ m. The ratio of the de Broglie wavelengths of the electron in the excited state to that in the ground state is:
sol: For a Bohr orbit, de Broglie wavelength = 2πr/n ∝ r/n. Third excited state is n = 4. Ratio = (r4/4)/(r1/1) = 8.48e−10/(4·5.3e−11) = 4.

q: A bob of mass m hangs from point O by a light string of length l and performs vertical circular motion. Given horizontal velocity v0 at the lowest point A, the string just becomes slack at the top point D. With B at 60° from A and C at 60° from D, the ratio of kinetic energies at B and C is:
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 250 240'><circle cx='120' cy='120' r='90' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='120' y1='30' x2='120' y2='210' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><line x1='120' y1='120' x2='198' y2='165' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='120' y1='120' x2='198' y2='75' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.2'/><circle cx='120' cy='120' r='2.5' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='104' y='118' font-size='12'>O</text><circle cx='120' cy='210' r='3' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='112' y='228' font-size='13'>A</text><circle cx='198' cy='165' r='3' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='204' y='169' font-size='13'>B</text><circle cx='198' cy='75' r='3' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='204' y='79' font-size='13'>C</text><circle cx='120' cy='30' r='3' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='112' y='26' font-size='13'>D</text><text x='140' y='158' font-size='10'>60</text><text x='140' y='96' font-size='10'>60</text><line x1='120' y1='210' x2='158' y2='210' stroke='#b91c1c' stroke-width='2'/><polygon points='158,210 151,206 151,214' fill='#b91c1c'/><text x='128' y='224' font-size='9'>v0</text></svg>
sol: At the top (slack), v_D² = gl, so KE_D = mgl/2 and KE_A = 5mgl/2. Heights: B is l/2 above A, C is 3l/2 above A. KE_B = 2mgl; KE_C = mgl. Ratio = 2.

q: A thin convex lens of glass (refractive index μ) has each side of radius of curvature R. One side is silvered for complete reflection. At what object distance on the optic axis does the image form on the object itself?
sol: The silvered lens acts as a mirror of equivalent power 2·P_lens + P_mirror = 2[2(μ−1)/R] + 2/R = 2(2μ−1)/R, so F = R/[2(2μ−1)]. The image coincides with the object at the centre of curvature, i.e. distance 2F = R/(2μ−1).

q: A point mass m is placed at distance 2R from the centre O of a big uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R; the gravitational force on it is F1. A spherical cavity of radius R/3 is removed (tangent to the near surface, centred toward m). The force on m due to the remaining part is F2. The ratio F1 : F2 is:
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 300 220'><circle cx='100' cy='110' r='80' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><text x='90' y='44' font-size='13'>M</text><circle cx='153' cy='110' r='27' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.4' stroke-dasharray='4 3'/><circle cx='100' cy='110' r='2.5' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='84' y='126' font-size='12'>O</text><circle cx='260' cy='110' r='3' fill='#b91c1c'/><text x='256' y='102' font-size='12'>P</text><text x='266' y='114' font-size='11'>m</text><line x1='100' y1='150' x2='260' y2='150' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='0.8'/><text x='168' y='165' font-size='10'>2R</text></svg>
sol: F1 = GMm/(2R)² = GMm/4R². Removed mass = M/27 with centre 2R/3 from O, so distance to m = 4R/3. Its force = G(M/27)m/(4R/3)² = GMm/48R². Then F2 = GMm/4R² − GMm/48R² = 11GMm/48R², giving F1:F2 = 12:11.

q: A closed organ tube and an open organ tube are filled with two gases of the same bulk modulus but different densities. The 9th harmonic of the closed tube matches the 4th harmonic of the open tube. The closed tube is 10 cm long and the gas density ratio (closed:open) is 1:16. The length of the open tube is:
sol: v = √(B/ρ), so v_closed/v_open = √16 = 4. Setting 9·v_closed/(4·L_closed) = 4·v_open/(2·L_open) with L_closed = 10 cm gives L_open = 20/9 cm.

q: If B is magnetic field and μ0 is permeability of free space, the dimensions of (B/μ0) are:
sol: [B] = [M T⁻² A⁻¹] and [μ0] = [M L T⁻² A⁻²], so [B/μ0] = [L⁻¹ A]. (This is the dimension of magnetic field strength H.)

q: A line charge of length a/2 is placed at the centre of an edge BC of a cube of edge length a. If the linear charge density is λ C/m, the total electric flux through all faces of the cube is (ε0 = free-space permittivity):
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 240 220'><polygon points='40,180 160,180 160,60 40,60' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='80,140 200,140 200,20 80,20' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='40' y1='180' x2='80' y2='140' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='160' y1='180' x2='200' y2='140' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='160' y1='60' x2='200' y2='20' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='40' y1='60' x2='80' y2='20' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.2'/><line x1='70' y1='180' x2='130' y2='180' stroke='#b91c1c' stroke-width='4'/><text x='92' y='198' font-size='11'>a/2 charge</text></svg>
sol: Total charge = λ·(a/2). A charge lying along an edge is symmetrically shared by 4 cubes (90° of 360°). So flux through this cube = ¼·λ·(a/2)/ε0 = λ·a/(8·ε0).

q: The work functions of caesium and lithium are 1.9 eV and 2.5 eV. If light of wavelength 550 nm is incident on both metal surfaces, the photoelectric effect is possible for:
sol: Photon energy = 1240/550 = 2.25 eV. This exceeds the work function of Cs (1.9 eV) but not of Li (2.5 eV), so emission occurs from Cs only.

q: Two spherical bodies of the same material have radii 0.2 m and 0.8 m. The smaller is at 800 K and the bigger at 400 K. If the energy radiated by the smaller body is E, the energy radiated by the bigger body is (surroundings negligible):
sol: Radiated power ∝ r²·T⁴. Ratio (big/small) = (0.8/0.2)²·(400/800)⁴ = 16·(1/16) = 1, so the bigger body radiates E.

q: Assertion (A): If Young's double slit experiment is performed in an optically denser medium than air, the consecutive fringes come closer. Reason (R): The speed of light reduces in a denser medium while its frequency does not change. Choose the most appropriate option:
o: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
sol: In a denser medium wavelength = λ/n decreases (speed drops, frequency unchanged), so fringe width β = λD/d decreases and fringes come closer. R correctly explains A.

q: A parallel-plate capacitor of 40 μF is connected to a 100 V supply. The gap is then filled with a dielectric of constant K = 2. The extra charge and the change in electrostatic energy, respectively, are:
sol: Initially Q = 4 mC, U = 0.2 J. After the dielectric, C doubles to 80 μF (supply connected), so Q = 8 mC and U = 0.4 J. Extra charge = 4 mC and energy change = 0.2 J.

q: Which resistivity-vs-temperature behaviour is most suitable for a wire-bound standard resistor?
o: Resistivity stays almost constant (negligible change) with temperature
sol: Standard resistors use alloys like manganin whose resistivity barely changes with temperature (very low temperature coefficient), so the near-constant curve is preferred.

q: A driver in a parked car watches a car approaching from behind in a convex side-view mirror of radius of curvature R = 2 m. The approaching car moves at 90 km/hr. When it is 24 m away, the magnitude of the acceleration of its image is 'a'. Find 100·a (in m/s²).
sol: For the convex mirror (f = +1 m), image position v = x/(x+1). Differentiating twice with dx/dt = −25 m/s gives image acceleration = 1250/(x+1)³. At x = 24: a = 1250/25³ = 0.08 m/s², so 100·a = 8.

q: Two soap bubbles of radii 2 cm and 4 cm are in contact with each other. The radius of curvature of the common surface, in cm, is ___
sol: Radius of common surface = r1·r2/(r2 − r1) = (2·4)/(4−2) = 4 cm.

q: Two 1 kg particles have position vectors rA = (a1·t² i + a2·t j + a3·t k) m and rB = (b1·t i + b2·t² j + b3·t k) m, with a1=1, a2=3n, a3=2, b1=2, b2=−1, b3=4p (SI units, n and p constants). At t = 1 s, |vA| = |vB| and vA ⊥ vB. At t = 1 s, the magnitude of the angular momentum of A about the position of B is √L kg m²/s. Find L.
sol: vA(1)=(2,3n,2), vB(1)=(2,−2,4p). Equal magnitudes give 9n²=16p²; perpendicularity gives 3n−4p=2. Solving: n=1/3, p=−1/4, so vA=(2,1,2). Positions rA=(1,1,2), rB=(2,−1,−1), relative r=(−1,2,3). L_vec = r×vA = (1,8,−5), magnitude √90. Hence L = 90.

q: Three conductors of the same length are connected as shown: conductors 1 (k1) and 2 (k2) in parallel between 100°C and a junction at θ, then conductor 3 (k3) from θ to 0°C. Conductors 1 and 2 have equal cross-section; conductor 3 has double that area. In steady state, θ (in °C) is ___ [k1 = 60, k2 = 120, k3 = 135 SI units].
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 300 180'><text x='12' y='30' font-size='12'>100 C</text><text x='140' y='30' font-size='12'>theta</text><text x='255' y='30' font-size='12'>0 C</text><rect x='55' y='45' width='95' height='35' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='95' y='67' font-size='12'>k1</text><rect x='55' y='100' width='95' height='35' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='95' y='122' font-size='12'>k2</text><rect x='150' y='58' width='100' height='65' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='192' y='95' font-size='12'>k3</text><line x1='45' y1='45' x2='45' y2='135' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='255' y1='58' x2='255' y2='123' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/></svg>
sol: Conductances: H1 = 60A/L, H2 = 120A/L (parallel = 180A/L); H3 = 135·(2A)/L = 270A/L. Steady state: 180(100 − θ) = 270θ, giving θ = 40°C.

q: A particle is projected at 30° from horizontal at 60 m/s. The height it rises in the first second is h0, and the height it rises in the last second before reaching maximum height is h1. Find the ratio h0 : h1. [g = 10 m/s²]
sol: Vertical velocity = 30 m/s, time to apex = 3 s. h0 = 30(1) − 5(1)² = 25 m. Height at t=3 is 45 m, at t=2 is 40 m, so h1 = 5 m. Ratio = 25:5 = 5.

q: From the five diode circuits shown (A–E, each with the indicated terminal voltages), identify which represent a forward-biased diode.
sol: A diode is forward biased when its p-side (anode) is at higher potential than its n-side (cathode). Applying this to the terminal voltages and orientations, circuits (B), (C) and (E) are forward biased. (Orientations are in the figure.)

q: A potentiometer wire has resistance Rp = 1 Ω and its sliding contact is at the middle. An external resistance Re = 2 Ω is connected via the sliding contact, and the supply is 0.9 V. The electric current in the circuit is:
sol: The slider splits the wire into two 0.5 Ω halves. One half (0.5 Ω) is in parallel with Re (2 Ω), giving 0.4 Ω; in series with the other half (0.5 Ω) gives 0.9 Ω total. Current = 0.9/0.9 = 1.0 A. (Wiring per the figure.)

q: In the arrangement shown, a glass lens (μ = 3/2) with surface radii R1 and R2 sits in a container with water (μ = 4/3) above and below it, forming three lenses. The power of the combination is:
sol: Adding the powers of the water-glass and glass-water interfaces (water μ = 4/3 above and below, glass μ = 3/2) and simplifying gives net power −(1/6)(1/|R1| − 1/|R2|). (Surface curvatures are in the figure.)

q: Statement I: Nitrogen, sulphur, halogen and phosphorus present in an organic compound are detected by Lassaigne's test. Statement II: The elements are converted from covalent to ionic form by fusing the compound with magnesium in Lassaigne's test. Choose the correct option:
o: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sol: Lassaigne's test detects N, S, halogens and P (Statement I true). But the fusion is done with sodium, not magnesium, so Statement II is false.

q: The density of a 3 M NaCl solution is 1.25 g/mL. The molality of the solution is:
sol: 1 L of solution has mass 1250 g and contains 3 mol NaCl = 175.5 g. Mass of water = 1074.5 g = 1.0745 kg. Molality = 3/1.0745 = 2.79 m.

q: The correct order of the following complexes in terms of increasing crystal field stabilization energy is:
sol: CFSE grows with more ligands, higher oxidation state and stronger field. So [Co(NH3)4]²⁺ (4 ligands, Co²⁺) < [Co(NH3)6]²⁺ (6 ligands, Co²⁺) < [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ (Co³⁺) < [Co(en)3]³⁺ (Co³⁺, stronger chelating en).

q: Statement I: Corrosion is an electrochemical phenomenon in which pure metal acts as an anode and impure metal as a cathode. Statement II: The rate of corrosion is more in alkaline medium than in acidic medium. Choose the correct option:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
sol: In corrosion the purer region behaves as anode and impure region as cathode (Statement I true). Corrosion is faster in acidic than alkaline media, so Statement II is false.

q: In the sequence RBr →(i) Mg, dry ether (ii) H2O→ 2-methylbutane, the maximum number of different RBr (structural isomers only) that can produce 2-methylbutane is:
sol: The Grignard route converts RBr to the alkane R-H, so R-H must be 2-methylbutane. The number of RBr equals the number of monobromo derivatives of 2-methylbutane, which has 4 distinct hydrogen environments, giving 4.

q: Which species does NOT undergo a disproportionation reaction?
sol: Disproportionation needs an intermediate oxidation state. In ClO4⁻ chlorine is at its maximum +7 and cannot be oxidised further, so it cannot disproportionate.

q: The molar solubility (s) of zirconium phosphate, Zr3(PO4)4, is given by:
sol: Zr3(PO4)4 dissolves to give 3 Zr⁴⁺ and 4 PO4³⁻. Ksp = (3s)³(4s)⁴ = 27·256·s⁷ = 6912 s⁷, so s = (Ksp/6912)^(1/7).

q: Identify the homoleptic complex(es) that is/are low spin: (A) [Fe(CN)5NO]²⁻, (B) [CoF6]³⁻, (C) [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻, (D) [Co(NH3)6]³⁺, (E) [Cr(H2O)6]²⁺.
sol: (A) is heteroleptic (CN and NO). Among the homoleptic ones, [Fe(CN)6]⁴⁻ (strong CN field) and [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ (Co³⁺ with NH3) are low spin, while [CoF6]³⁻ and [Cr(H2O)6]²⁺ are high spin.

q: Match List I (partial derivatives) with List II. List I: (A) (∂G/∂T)P, (B) (∂H/∂T)P, (C) (∂G/∂P)T, (D) (∂U/∂T)V. List II: (I) Cp, (II) −S, (III) Cv, (IV) V.
sol: (∂G/∂T)P = −S, (∂H/∂T)P = Cp, (∂G/∂P)T = V, (∂U/∂T)V = Cv. So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

q: Statement I: A spectral line will be observed for a 2px → 2py transition. Statement II: 2px and 2py are degenerate orbitals. Choose the correct option:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sol: 2px and 2py have the same energy (degenerate), so Statement II is true. A transition between orbitals of equal energy involves no energy change and gives no spectral line, so Statement I is false.

q: Statement I: An element at the extreme left of the periodic table forms acidic oxides. Statement II: An acid is formed when water reacts with the oxide of a reactive element at the extreme right of the periodic table. Choose the correct option:
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sol: Extreme-left elements (alkali metals) form basic oxides, so Statement I is false. Reactive non-metals on the extreme right give acidic oxides that form acids with water (e.g., Cl2O7 → HClO4), so Statement II is true.

q: Toluene (excess) is treated with (i) CrO2Cl2 in CS2, (ii) H3O⁺, (iii) NaHSO3 to give residue (A). Then (A) + dilute HCl gives compound (B). The structures of (A) and (B), respectively, are:
sol: This is the Etard reaction: toluene gives benzaldehyde. With NaHSO3 the aldehyde forms the sodium bisulfite addition compound PhCH(OH)SO3Na (A). Dilute HCl regenerates benzaldehyde PhCHO (B).

q: Which alkane has exactly two secondary hydrogens?
sol: In 2,2,3,3-tetramethylpentane, C2 and C3 are quaternary and the terminal methyls are primary; only the single CH2 (C4) is a secondary carbon, giving exactly two secondary hydrogens.

q: Which is the most stable carbocation?
sol: A para-methoxy group donates electron density by resonance directly onto the benzylic carbon, giving the greatest stabilization. So the para-methoxybenzyl cation is most stable.

q: Match the compounds (List I) with the reagents (List II) for reduction to the corresponding amines. List I: (A) amide R-CO-NH2, (B) nitrobenzene, (C) nitrile R-C≡N, (D) an N-substituted phthalimide. List II: (I) NaOH (aqueous), (II) H2/Ni, (III) LiAlH4 then H2O, (IV) Sn/HCl.
sol: Amide → amine with LiAlH4 (III); nitrobenzene → aniline with Sn/HCl (IV); nitrile → amine with H2/Ni (II); N-substituted phthalimide → amine on NaOH hydrolysis (I). So A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

q: Arrange the following in increasing order of dipole moment: HBr, H2S, NF3, CHCl3.
sol: Approximate dipole moments: NF3 (0.24 D) < HBr (0.79 D) < H2S (0.97 D) < CHCl3 (1.04 D). NF3 is low because the N lone pair opposes the N-F bond dipoles.

q: The maximum covalency of a non-metallic group-15 element 'E' having the weakest E-E single bond is:
sol: Nitrogen has the weakest E-E single bond in group 15 (lone-pair repulsion). Lacking d-orbitals, nitrogen's maximum covalency is 4 (as in NH4⁺).

q: A compound with molecular formula C6H6 gives only one monobromo derivative and takes up four moles of hydrogen per mole for complete hydrogenation. The number of pi electrons it contains is ___
sol: Taking up 4 moles of H2 means the molecule has 4 pi bonds (no ring, unlike benzene which takes 3). Four pi bonds correspond to 8 pi electrons.

q: 20 mL of 2 M NaOH is added to 400 mL of 0.5 M NaOH. The final concentration of the solution is ___ ×10⁻² M. (nearest integer)
sol: Total moles = 0.04 + 0.20 = 0.24 mol in 420 mL. Concentration = 0.24/0.42 = 0.571 M = 57×10⁻² M.

q: Given: C2H6(g) + 7/2 O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O, ΔH1 = −1550; C(graphite) + O2 → CO2, ΔH2 = −393.5; H2 + 1/2 O2 → H2O, ΔH3 = −286 (all kJ/mol). The magnitude of the standard enthalpy of formation of C2H6(g) is ___ kJ/mol. (nearest integer)
Niobium (Nb) and ruthenium (Ru) have x and y electrons respectively in their 4d orbitals. The value of x + y is ___
sol: Nb (Z=41): [Kr] 4d⁴ 5s¹, so x = 4. Ru (Z=44): [Kr] 4d⁷ 5s¹, so y = 7. Thus x + y = 11.

q: The complex of Ni²⁺ ion with dimethylglyoxime contains ___ hydrogen (H) atoms.
sol: In Ni(dmgH)2 each dimethylglyoximate ligand (from C4H8N2O2) loses one proton to give dmgH⁻ with 7 hydrogens. Two such ligands contribute 2×7 = 14 H atoms.

q: From the given energy-vs-reaction-coordinate diagram (activated complex at the top, with E1 and E2 marked on descent toward the product), choose the correct option:
o: Activation energy of both forward and backward reaction is E1+E2 and reactant is more stable than product
Activation energy of the forward reaction is E1+E2 and product is less stable than reactant
Activation energy of the backward reaction is E1 and product is more stable than reactant
Activation energy of the forward reaction is E1+E2 and product is more stable than reactant
sol: The forward activation energy is the full rise from reactant to activated complex (E1+E2), and since the product sits higher than the reactant, the product is less stable. (E1/E2 defined in the figure.)

q: Identify the number of structures (from the four Fischer projections shown) that can be correlated to D-glyceraldehyde.
sol: Comparing the configuration at the reference carbon with that of D-glyceraldehyde, three of the four drawn structures correlate to the D-configuration. (Structures are in the figure.)

q: When sec-butylcyclohexane reacts with bromine in the presence of sunlight, the major product results from bromination at which position?
o: a primary carbon of the ethyl group
a ring CH2 adjacent to the substituent
the tertiary carbon joining the sec-butyl group to the ring
an internal CH2 of the butyl chain
sol: Free-radical bromination is highly selective for the most stable radical. The carbon linking the sec-butyl group to the ring is tertiary, so bromination there gives the major product. (Exact structures are in the figure.)

q: The radius of the first excited state of the He+ ion is given as (a0 = radius of the first stationary state of the hydrogen atom):
sol: Bohr radius r = a0·n²/Z. For He+ (Z=2) in the first excited state (n=2): r = a0·4/2 = 2a0.

q: The incorrect statements regarding geometrical isomerism are: (A) Propene shows geometrical isomerism. (B) A trans isomer has identical atoms/groups on opposite sides of the double bond. (C) Cis-but-2-ene has a higher dipole moment than trans-but-2-ene. (D) 2-methylbut-2-ene shows two geometrical isomers. (E) A trans isomer has a lower melting point than the cis isomer. Choose the correct answer:
sol: Propene (A) has no geometrical isomerism (terminal =CH2). 2-methylbut-2-ene (D) has two identical methyls on one alkene carbon, so no GI. Trans isomers usually have higher melting points, so (E) is wrong. Hence (A), (D), (E) are the incorrect statements.

q: A liquid kept in a thermally insulated closed vessel at 25°C is mechanically stirred from outside. The correct thermodynamic parameters are:
sol: Thermally insulated means q = 0. Stirring does work on the system, so w > 0. Then ΔU = q + w > 0.

q: Which of the following electronegativity orders is incorrect?
sol: Magnesium (≈1.31) is less electronegative than aluminium (≈1.61), so 'Al < Mg' is wrong; the correct order is Mg < Al. The other three orders are correct.

q: Lanthanoid ions with a 4f⁷ configuration are: (A) Eu²⁺, (B) Gd³⁺, (C) Eu³⁺, (D) Tb³⁺, (E) Sm²⁺. Choose the correct answer:
sol: Eu²⁺ ([Xe]4f⁷) and Gd³⁺ ([Xe]4f⁷) both have the half-filled 4f⁷ configuration. Eu³⁺ is 4f⁶, Tb³⁺ is 4f⁸, and Sm²⁺ is 4f⁶.

q: Statement I: One mole of propyne reacts with excess sodium to liberate half a mole of H2 gas. Statement II: Four grams of propyne reacts with NaNH2 to liberate NH3 that occupies 224 mL at STP. Choose the most appropriate answer:
o: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
sol: Propyne has one acidic terminal H, so 1 mol gives ½ mol H2 (I correct). 4 g propyne = 0.1 mol, releasing 0.1 mol NH3 = 2240 mL at STP, not 224 mL, so Statement II is incorrect.

q: Which compounds give a positive Fehling's test? (A) benzaldehyde, (B) acetophenone (PhCOCH3), (C) a ketohexose HOCH2-CO-(CHOH)3-CH2OH, (D) acetaldehyde (CH3CHO), (E) phenylacetaldehyde (PhCH2CHO).
sol: Fehling's is positive for aliphatic aldehydes and reducing sugars. Acetaldehyde (D), phenylacetaldehyde (E) and the ketohexose (C) test positive; aromatic benzaldehyde (A) and the ketone acetophenone (B) do not.

q: Which electrolyte is used to obtain H2S2O8 (peroxydisulfuric acid) by electrolysis?
o: Acidified dilute solution of sodium sulphate
sol: Peroxydisulfuric acid (Marshall's acid) is formed by electrolysis of concentrated sulphuric acid at high current density, where bisulfate ions are oxidised and couple.

q: Statement I: CH3-O-CH2-Cl undergoes an SN1 reaction even though it is a primary halide. Statement II: Neopentyl chloride (CH3)3C-CH2-Cl does not undergo SN2 easily even though it is a primary halide. Choose the most appropriate answer:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
sol: The adjacent oxygen stabilises the carbocation (oxocarbenium ion), so CH3-O-CH2-Cl can go SN1 (I correct). The bulky tert-butyl group in neopentyl chloride blocks backside attack, hindering SN2 (II correct).

q: Which of the following acids is a vitamin?
sol: Ascorbic acid is vitamin C.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: (A) Al³⁺ < Mg²⁺ < Na⁺ < F⁻, (B) B < C < O < N, (C) B < Al < Mg < K, (D) Si < P < S < Cl. List II: (I) Ionisation Enthalpy, (II) Metallic character, (III) Electronegativity, (IV) Ionic radii.
sol: (A) is an isoelectronic series in increasing ionic radii (IV). (B) is increasing ionisation enthalpy (I), with N > O. (C) is increasing metallic character (II). (D) is increasing electronegativity (III).

q: Which statement is NOT true for radioactive decay?
o: Decay constant increases with increase in temperature
The amount remaining after three half-lives is 1/8 of the original
Decay constant does not depend on temperature
Half-life equals ln2 divided by the rate constant
sol: The decay constant is a nuclear property, independent of temperature, so the claim that it increases with temperature is not true.

q: Nitrobenzene is treated with (i) Br2/AcOH, (ii) Sn/HCl, (iii) NaNO2/HCl at 273 K, (iv) C2H5OH. The products formed (A + B) are:
sol: Bromination gives m-bromonitrobenzene; Sn/HCl reduces it to 3-bromoaniline; diazotisation gives the diazonium salt; ethanol reduces (deaminates) it to bromobenzene while being oxidised to acetaldehyde. So A = bromobenzene, B = CH3CHO.

q: How many different stereoisomers are possible for CH3-CH(OH)-CH=CH-CH3 (pent-3-en-2-ol)?
sol: There is one chiral centre (C2, giving 2 configurations) and one C=C double bond (giving E/Z, 2 configurations). Total = 2 × 2 = 4 stereoisomers.

q: A vessel at 1000 K contains CO2 at 0.5 atm. Some CO2 converts to CO on adding graphite. If the total pressure at equilibrium is 0.8 atm, then Kp is:
sol: CO2 + C ⇌ 2CO. Let x react: total = 0.5 + x = 0.8, so x = 0.3. Then CO2 = 0.2, CO = 0.6. Kp = (0.6)²/0.2 = 1.8 atm.

q: A solution of aluminium chloride is electrolysed for 30 minutes with a current of 2 A. The mass of aluminium deposited at the cathode is (molar mass Al = 27, F = 96500 C/mol):
The IUPAC name of the compound CH3-CH(COOH)-CH2-CH2-CH(COOCH3)-CH3 is:
sol: The molecule is the mono-methyl ester of 2,5-dimethylhexanedioic acid. Taking –COOH as the senior group and the ester as a methoxycarbonyl substituent gives 6-methoxycarbonyl-2,5-dimethylhexanoic acid.

q: In which complex is the crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) equal to zero?
sol: K3[Fe(SCN)6] has Fe³⁺ (d⁵) with the weak-field ligand SCN, giving a high-spin d⁵ configuration whose CFSE is zero. The others (low-spin d⁵ or d⁶) have non-zero CFSE.

q: Arrange the following in increasing order of boiling points: (i) 10⁻⁴ M NaCl, (ii) 10⁻⁴ M urea, (iii) 10⁻³ M NaCl, (iv) 10⁻² M NaCl.
sol: Boiling-point elevation depends on effective particle concentration (i × molality; i = 2 for NaCl, 1 for urea). Effective values: urea 10⁻⁴ < NaCl 2×10⁻⁴ < NaCl 2×10⁻³ < NaCl 2×10⁻², giving (ii) < (i) < (iii) < (iv).

q: From the magnetic behaviour of [NiCl4]²⁻ (paramagnetic) and [Ni(CO)4] (diamagnetic), the correct geometry and oxidation state are:
o: [NiCl4]²⁻: Ni(II) square planar; [Ni(CO)4]: Ni(0) square planar
sol: [NiCl4]²⁻ is Ni(II) (d⁸) with weak-field Cl⁻: paramagnetic and tetrahedral. [Ni(CO)4] is Ni(0) (d¹⁰) with strong-field CO: diamagnetic and tetrahedral.

q: The number of molecules/ions that show linear geometry among the following is ___ : SO2, BeCl2, CO2, N3⁻, NO2, F2O, XeF2, NO2⁺, I3⁻, O3.
sol: Linear species (180°): BeCl2, CO2, N3⁻, XeF2, NO2⁺ and I3⁻ = 6. SO2, NO2, F2O and O3 are bent.

q: A → B follows first-order kinetics at 1000 K. If the activation barrier is 191.48 kJ/mol and the frequency factor is 10²⁰, the time required for 50% of A to convert to B is ___ picoseconds (nearest integer). [R = 8.314 J/K/mol]
Nitrobenzene is treated with (i) Sn + HCl, (ii) NaNO2/HCl at 0°C, (iii) Cu2Cl2, (iv) Na/ether to give product A. The molar mass of A is ___ g/mol.
sol: Nitrobenzene → aniline → benzenediazonium chloride → chlorobenzene (Sandmeyer) → biphenyl (Fittig coupling with Na). Biphenyl C12H10 has molar mass 154 g/mol.

q: CO2 gas at 1 atm and 273 K is passed through a Ca(OH)2 solution. The excess unreacted Ca(OH)2 is neutralised with 40 mL of 0.1 M HCl. If the CO2 reacted with exactly half of the initial Ca(OH)2, the volume of the CO2 container was x cm³. Find x (nearest integer).
sol: Moles HCl = 0.004; excess Ca(OH)2 = 0.004/2 = 0.002 mol = half the initial, so initial Ca(OH)2 = 0.004 mol and CO2 reacted = 0.002 mol. At STP, V = 0.002·22400 = 44.8 cm³ ≈ 45 cm³.

q: In the Carius method, 180 mg of an organic compound produced 143.5 mg of AgCl. The percentage of chlorine in the compound is ___ % (Ag = 108, Cl = 35.5).
If the first term of an A.P. is 3 and the sum of its first four terms equals one-fifth of the sum of the next four terms, then the sum of the first 20 terms is:
One die has faces marked 1,1,2,2,3,4 and another has faces marked 1,2,2,3,3,4. The probability of getting a sum of 4 or 5 when both are thrown is:
sol: Over all 36 equally likely pairs, 18 give a sum of 4 or 5, so the probability is 18/36 = 1/2.

q: A tetrahedron ABCD has A, B, C at position vectors i+2j+k, i+3j−2k and 2i+j−k. The altitude from D to face ABC meets the median through A of triangle ABC at E. If AD = √110/3 and the volume is √805/(6√2), the position vector of E is:
sol: E lies on the median from A to the midpoint of BC, i.e. A + t(mid(BC)−A). Fixing t with the given AD length and volume gives E = (1/6)(7i + 12j + k).

q: If A, B and (adj(A⁻¹) + adj(B⁻¹)) are non-singular matrices of the same order, then the inverse of A(adj(A⁻¹) + adj(B⁻¹))⁻¹B is:
sol: Using adj(M⁻¹) = M/|M| and inverting the product, the expression simplifies to (1/|AB|)(adj(B) + adj(A)).

q: In a grouped frequency distribution with equal class widths, the median is 14 with median class 12–18 and median-class frequency 12. If the number of students with marks less than 12 is 18, the total number of students is:
A curve y = f(x) passes through (0, 5) and (ln 2, k) and satisfies 2(3 + y)e^(2x) dx − (7 + e^(2x)) dy = 0. Then k equals:
sol: Separating variables gives 3 + y = A(7 + e^(2x)); using (0,5) gives A = 1, so y = 4 + e^(2x). At x = ln 2, e^(2x) = 4, so k = 8.

q: If f(x) = (2/x)[sin((k1+1)x) + sin((k2−1)x)] for x<0, f(0)=4, and f(x) = (2/x)·ln((2+k1·x)/(2+k2·x)) for x>0 is continuous at x=0, then k1² + k2² equals:
sol: Left limit = 2(k1 + k2), right limit = k1 − k2. Continuity with f(0)=4 gives k1 + k2 = 2 and k1 − k2 = 4, so k1 = 3, k2 = −1 and k1² + k2² = 10.

q: If the line 3x − 2y + 12 = 0 intersects the parabola 4y = 3x² at points A and B, then at the vertex of the parabola the segment AB subtends an angle equal to:
sol: Solving gives A = (4, 12) and B = (−2, 3). Slopes from the vertex are m1 = 3, m2 = −3/2, so tan(angle) = |(m1 − m2)/(1 + m1·m2)| = 9/7, i.e. arctan(9/7).

q: Let P be the foot of the perpendicular from Q(10,−3,−1) to the line (x−3)/7 = (y−2)/(−1) = (z+1)/(−2). The area of the right-angled triangle PQR, where R = (3,−2,1), is:
sol: The foot of the perpendicular is P = (10, 1, −3). The triangle is right-angled at P, and area = ½|PQ × PR| = 3√30.

q: Arc AC of a circle subtends a right angle at the centre O. Point B on arc AC divides it so that (arc AB)/(arc BC) = 1/5. If OC = a·OA + b·OB (vectors), then a + √2·(√3 − 1)·b equals:
sol: Angle AOB = 15°, BOC = 75°. Taking OA at 0° and OC at 90°, solving OC = a·OA + b·OB gives a = −cot15°, b = 1/sin15°. The expression evaluates to 2 − √3.

q: Let f(x) = ln x and g(x) = (x⁴ − 2x³ + 3x² − 2x + 2)/(2x² − 2x + 1). Then the domain of f∘g is:
sol: The denominator 2x² − 2x + 1 is always positive, and the numerator is always positive (minimum ≈ 1.56), so g(x) > 0 for all x. Hence the domain of ln(g(x)) is all of R.

q: If the system (L−1)x + (L−4)y + Lz = 5, Lx + (L−1)y + (L−4)z = 7, (L+1)x + (L+2)y − (L+2)z = 9 has infinitely many solutions, then L² + L equals:
sol: The coefficient determinant vanishes for L = −1/2 or L = 3. Checking consistency selects L = 3, giving L² + L = 12.

q: The number of words formed using all the letters of 'DAUGHTER' so that all the vowels never come together is:
sol: Total arrangements = 8! = 40320. Arrangements with the 3 vowels together = 6!·3! = 4320. Never together = 40320 − 4320 = 36000.

q: Let R = {(1,2),(2,3),(3,3)} be a relation on {1,2,3,4}. The minimum number of ordered pairs to add so that R becomes an equivalence relation is:
sol: An equivalence relation here makes {1,2,3} one class (9 ordered pairs) plus (4,4), i.e. 10 pairs. Three already exist, so 7 must be added.

q: Triangle PQR has P(5,4), Q(−2,4), R(a,b) with area 35. If its orthocentre is (2, 14/5) and centroid is (c,d), then c + 2d equals:
sol: The orthocentre conditions give R = (2, −6). The centroid is (5/3, 2/3), so c + 2d = 5/3 + 4/3 = 3.

q: The value of ∫ from e² to e⁴ of (1/x)·[ e^(1/((ln x)²+1)) / ( e^(1/((ln x)²+1)) + e^(1/((6−ln x)²+1)) ) ] dx is:
sol: Substituting t = ln x maps the limits to 2 and 4, and the integrand f(t) satisfies f(t) + f(6 − t) = 1 (symmetric about t = 3). So the integral = (4 − 2)/2 = 1.

q: Let |(conj(z) − i)/(2·conj(z) + i)| = 1/3, z ∈ C, describe a circle with centre C. If the area of the triangle with vertices (0,0), C and (a,0) is 11, then a² equals:
sol: The locus reduces to x² + y² + (22/5)y + 8/5 = 0 with centre C = (0, −11/5). Area = ½|a|·(11/5) = 11 gives |a| = 10, so a² = 100.

q: The value of (sin 70°)·(cot 10°·cot 70° − 1) is:
sol: Simplifying using product-to-sum identities, (sin 70°)(cot 10°·cot 70° − 1) = 1.

q: For π/2 ≤ x ≤ 3π/4, arccos((12/13)cos x + (5/13)sin x) equals:
sol: Writing 12/13 = cos p, 5/13 = sin p with p = arctan(5/12), the argument is cos(x − p). Since x − p lies in [0, π], arccos(cos(x − p)) = x − arctan(5/12).

q: A circle C touches the line x − y + 1 = 0, has its centre on the positive x-axis, and cuts a chord of length 4/√13 along the line −3x + 2y = 1. A hyperbola H: x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 has one focus at the centre of C and transverse-axis length equal to the diameter of C. Then 2a² + 3b² equals ___
sol: The centre is (3,0) with radius 2√2. So a = 2√2, focus c = 3, and b² = c² − a² = 1. Then 2a² + 3b² = 16 + 3 = 19.

q: If a(b−c)x² + b(c−a)x + c(a−b) = 0 has equal roots, where a + c = 15 and b = 36/5, then a² + c² equals ___
sol: x = 1 is always a root; equal roots require 2ac = b(a + c). With a + c = 15 and b = 36/5, ac = 54, so {a,c} = {6,9} and a² + c² = 117.

q: If the set of all values of a for which 5x³ − 15x − a = 0 has three distinct real roots is the interval (α, β), then β − 2α equals ___
sol: f(x) = 5x³ − 15x has local max 10 at x = −1 and local min −10 at x = 1. Three roots require a ∈ (−10, 10), so α = −10, β = 10 and β − 2α = 30.

q: The area of the larger portion bounded between the curves x² + y² = 25 and y = |x − 1| is (1/4)(b·π + c) with b, c natural numbers. Then b + c equals ___
sol: The V-shaped line y = |x−1| cuts the circle; the larger region has area (1/4)(75π + 2), so b = 75, c = 2 and b + c = 77.

q: A spherical surface of radius R separates air from glass (n = 1.5), with the centre of curvature in the glass. A point object O in air forms a real image I in glass, and the line OI meets the surface at P with PO = PI. The distance PO equals:
sol: Using n2/v − n1/u = (n2 − n1)/R with u = −d, v = +d (PO = PI = d), R = +R: 1.5/d + 1/d = 0.5/R gives 2.5/d = 0.5/R, so d = 5R.

q: The position of a particle on the x-axis is x(t) = A sin t + B cos²t + C t² + D. The dimension of ABC/D is:
sol: Each term has dimension of length, so A = L, B = L, C = L T⁻², D = L. Then ABC/D = (L)(L)(L T⁻²)/L = L² T⁻².

q: A thin convex lens (refractive index μ2) is kept in a liquid (refractive index μ1, with μ1 < μ2), with radii of curvature |R1| and |R2|. Its second surface is silvered. Where should an object be placed on the optic axis so that a real, inverted image forms at the same place?
sol: The silvered lens acts as a mirror of power P = 2·P_lens + P_mirror, with P_lens = ((μ2−μ1)/μ1)(1/|R1|+1/|R2|) and P_mirror = 2/|R2|. The object at 2/P simplifies to μ1|R1||R2| / (μ2(|R1|+|R2|) − μ1|R2|).

q: Statement I: Hot water flows faster than cold water. Statement II: Soap water has higher surface tension than fresh water. Choose the correct option:
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
sol: Hot water has lower viscosity, so it flows faster (I true). Soap is a surfactant and lowers surface tension, so Statement II is false.

q: A circular disc of radius 20 cm is centred at the origin. A circular hole of radius 5 cm is cut so that the edge of the hole touches the edge of the disc. The distance of the centre of mass of the remaining disc from the origin is:
sol: The hole's centre is at 20 − 5 = 15 cm. Shift = (hole area × 15)/(disc area − hole area) = (25 × 15)/(400 − 25) = 375/375 = 1.0 cm.

q: The electric flux is φ = a·σ + b·λ, where σ and λ are surface and linear charge density respectively. Then (a/b) represents:
sol: a = φ/σ and b = φ/λ, so a/b = λ/σ = (C/m)/(C/m²) = m, a length (displacement).

q: A subatomic particle of mass 10⁻³⁰ kg moves at 2.21×10⁶ m/s. Under matter-wave consideration, it behaves closely like (h = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ J·s):
sol: de Broglie wavelength = h/(mv) = 6.63e−34/(1e−30 × 2.21e6) = 3×10⁻¹⁰ m = 3 Å, which lies in the X-ray range.

q: For a moving coil galvanometer: A. The torsional constant has dimensions [M L² T⁻²]. B. Increasing current sensitivity may not necessarily increase voltage sensitivity. C. Doubling the turns N to 2N doubles the voltage sensitivity. D. It becomes an ammeter by adding a large shunt resistance in parallel. E. Current sensitivity depends inversely on the number of turns. Choose the correct set:
sol: A correct (kθ = torque, so k is [ML²T⁻²]). B correct (more turns raises resistance, so voltage sensitivity NBA/kR may not rise). C false (R also roughly doubles). D false (shunt is small). E false (current sensitivity ∝ N). So A and B only.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: (A) Pressure varies inversely with volume of an ideal gas; (B) Heat absorbed goes partly to internal energy and partly to work; (C) Heat is neither absorbed nor released; (D) No work is done on or by a gas. List II: (I) Adiabatic; (II) Isochoric; (III) Isothermal; (IV) Isobaric.
sol: PV = const is isothermal (III); heat split between internal energy and work is isobaric (IV); no heat exchange is adiabatic (I); no work is isochoric (II).

q: The electric field of an EM wave in free space is E = 57 cos[7.5×10⁶ t − 5×10⁻³(3x + 4y)](4i − 3j) N/C. The associated magnetic field (in tesla) is:
sol: Propagation is along (3i+4j)/5. B = (1/c)(k̂ × E). Here k̂ × E = −285 k, so B = −(285/3×10⁸) k = −(57/3×10⁸)(5k) cos[…].

q: A lead bullet at 300 K enters a wooden block and just melts (melting point 600 K). If the total heat required is 625 J, the mass of the bullet is (latent heat of fusion = 2.5×10⁴ J/kg, specific heat = 125 J/kg/K):
The lateral shift of a ray refracted through a parallel-sided glass slab of thickness h, in terms of angle of incidence i and refraction r (slab in air), is:
sol: The standard lateral displacement of a ray through a parallel slab is h·sin(i − r)/cos r.

q: A radioactive nucleus n2 has 3 times the decay constant of another nucleus n1. With equal initial numbers, the ratio of the number of nuclei of n2 to n1 after one half-life of n1 is:
A light hollow cube of side 10 cm and mass 10 g floats in water. Pushed down and released, it executes SHM with period y·π×10⁻² s. Find y (g = 10 m/s², density of water = 10³ kg/m³):

Regarding self-inductance: A. It depends on the coil's geometry. B. It does not depend on the permeability of the medium. C. Self-induced emf opposes any change in current. D. It is the electromagnetic analogue of mass. E. Work must be done against the self-induced emf while establishing the current. Choose the correct set:
sol: Self-inductance depends on geometry (A) and on permeability, so B is false. C, D and E are correct. Hence A, C, D, E.

q: From the velocity-time graph (velocity rises linearly from 200 m/s at t=0 to 400 m/s at t=2 s, then stays constant at 400 m/s), the distance covered by the airplane in the first 30.5 s is:
