q: For the series circuit (5 V battery, resistor R, key, and a capacitor with plates A and B), identify the valid statements at the instant the key is closed: A. No current through R. B. Maximum current in the connecting wires. C. Potential difference between plates A and B is minimum. D. Charge on the plates is minimum. Choose the correct set:
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 300 170'><rect x='40' y='30' width='220' height='110' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><path d='M120 30 l8 -6 l8 12 l8 -12 l8 12 l8 -6' fill='none' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='120' y='20' font-size='11'>R</text><line x1='185' y1='24' x2='185' y2='36' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><line x1='185' y1='30' x2='205' y2='22' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><text x='188' y='16' font-size='10'>Key</text><line x1='230' y1='78' x2='250' y2='78' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='230' y1='92' x2='250' y2='92' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><text x='255' y='88' font-size='10'>5V</text><line x1='40' y1='78' x2='55' y2='78' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><line x1='40' y1='92' x2='55' y2='92' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='2'/><text x='24' y='75' font-size='10'>A</text><text x='24' y='104' font-size='10'>B</text></svg>
sol: At the instant of closing, the uncharged capacitor behaves as a short: current is maximum in the wires (B), the plate voltage is minimum (C), and the charge is minimum (D). Current does flow through R, so A is false.

q: A solid sphere rolls without slipping down an incline of length L at 30°, reaching the bottom with speed v1. If the angle is increased to 45° (L constant), the new speed is v2. The ratio v1² : v2² is:
sol: For rolling, v² = (10/7)gL·sinθ. So v1² : v2² = sin30° : sin45° = (1/2) : (1/√2) = 1 : √2.

q: A positive ion A (charge 6.67×10⁻¹⁹ C, mass 19.2×10⁻²⁷ kg) and a negative ion B (charge 9.6×10⁻¹⁰ C, mass 9×10⁻²⁷ kg) are separated by distance r. The ratio of electrostatic to gravitational force is P×10⁴⁵. Find 10P. (1/4πε0 = 9×10⁹, G = 6.67×10⁻¹¹)
In a circuit with a 3 H inductor, a 12 V battery and a variable resistor R, the sliding contact is pulled outward so the current changes at 8 A/s. When R = 12 Ω, the current in the circuit is ___ A.
sol: KVL: 12 = I·R + L·(dI/dt). Pulling the contact out increases R, so dI/dt = −8 A/s: 12 = 12I − 3×8, giving 12I = 36 and I = 3 A.

q: Two particles are at equal distances from the origin with position vectors A = 2i + 3n·j + 2k and B = 2i − 2j + 4p·k. If the vectors are perpendicular to each other, the value of n⁻¹ is ___
sol: Equal magnitudes give 9n² = 16p²; perpendicularity gives 4 − 6n + 8p = 0. Solving gives n = 1/3, so n⁻¹ = 3.

q: An ideal gas at 0°C is suddenly compressed to one-fourth of its volume. If Cp/Cv = 3/2, the change in temperature due to the process is ___ K.
Statement I: Fructose has no aldehydic group but still reduces Tollen's reagent. Statement II: In the presence of base, fructose rearranges to give glucose. Choose the correct option:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sol: Fructose (a ketose) isomerises to glucose/mannose under basic conditions (Lobry de Bruyn rearrangement) and so reduces Tollen's reagent. Both statements are true.

q: The complex that shows facial-meridional (fac-mer) isomerism is:
sol: fac-mer isomerism requires an octahedral MA3B3 complex. Only [Co(NH3)3Cl3] fits this type.

q: Given the reduction potentials FeO4²⁻ → Fe³⁺ (+2.0 V), Fe³⁺ → Fe²⁺ (0.8 V), Fe²⁺ → Fe⁰ (−0.5 V), the value of E°(FeO4²⁻/Fe²⁺) is:
sol: Combining via free energies (3 electrons for +6→+3, 1 for +3→+2): E = (3·2.0 + 1·0.8)/4 = 6.8/4 = 1.7 V.

q: The element that does NOT belong to the same period as the others is:
sol: Ir (77), Pt (78) and Os (76) are period-6 (5d) elements, whereas Pd (46) is a period-5 (4d) element.

q: Match List I (octet classification) with List II (examples). List I: (A) obeying octet rule; (B) incomplete octet; (C) incomplete octet with odd electron; (D) expanded octet. List II: (I) NO, NO2; (II) BCl3, AlCl3; (III) H2SO4, PCl5; (IV) CCl4, CO2.
sol: CCl4/CO2 obey the octet (IV); BCl3/AlCl3 have incomplete octet (II); NO/NO2 are odd-electron with incomplete octet (I); H2SO4/PCl5 have expanded octet (III).

q: What mass of bromine is required to convert 2 g of phenol into 2,4,6-tribromophenol? (molar masses: C=12, H=1, O=16, Br=80)
sol: Phenol (M = 94) reacts with 3 Br2. Mass = 3·(2/94)·160 = 10.21 g.

q: Which of the following react with Hinsberg's reagent? (A) aniline; (B) N,N-dimethylaniline; (C) methylamine (CH3-NH2); (D) trimethylamine N(CH3)3; (E) diphenylamine (C6H5-NH-C6H5).
sol: Hinsberg's reagent (benzenesulfonyl chloride) reacts with primary and secondary amines only. Aniline (1°), methylamine (1°) and diphenylamine (2°) react; the tertiary amines B and D do not.

q: The correct set of aqueous ions having a similar colour is:
sol: V²⁺ and Cr³⁺ (both d³) with Mn³⁺ give a similar violet colouration; the other sets mix colourless and differently coloured ions.

q: Statement I: In Lassaigne's test, covalent organic molecules are transformed into ionic compounds. Statement II: The sodium fusion extract of a compound having both N and S gives a Prussian-blue colour with FeSO4 and Na4[Fe(CN)6]. Choose the correct option:
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sol: Fusion with sodium converts covalent species to ionic ones (I true). When N and S are both present, sodium thiocyanate forms, giving a blood-red (not Prussian-blue) test, so Statement II is false.

q: Propane on photochemical chlorination gives two dichloro products x and y, of which x is optically active. How many trichloro products (structural isomers) are obtained from x on further chlorination?
sol: The optically active dichloride x is 1,2-dichloropropane (CH2Cl-CHCl-CH3). A further Cl at C1, C2 or C3 gives three structural trichloro isomers (1,1,2-, 1,2,2- and 1,2,3-trichloropropane).

q: CrCl3·xNH3 exists as a complex. A 0.1 molal aqueous solution shows a freezing-point depression of 0.558°C. Assuming 100% ionisation and Cr coordination number 6, the complex is (Kf = 1.86 K·kg/mol):
sol: i = ΔTf/(Kf·m) = 0.558/(1.86·0.1) = 3, so the complex gives 3 ions. [Cr(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 (one complex cation + 2 Cl⁻) fits, with coordination number 6.

q: When NH4OH is added gradually to a solution containing 1 M A²⁺ and 1 M B³⁺ (Ksp[A(OH)2] = 9×10⁻¹⁰, Ksp[B(OH)3] = 27×10⁻¹⁸ at 298 K), then:
o: Both A(OH)2 and B(OH)3 do not precipitate
sol: A(OH)2 needs [OH⁻] = 3×10⁻⁵; B(OH)3 needs [OH⁻] = 3×10⁻⁶. Since B(OH)3 requires a lower OH⁻ concentration, it precipitates first.

q: The major product of the reaction of CH3CH2CHO with excess HCHO in alkali (reflux) is:
sol: The two α-hydrogens of propanal undergo crossed aldol with formaldehyde, then the remaining CHO is reduced by excess HCHO via crossed Cannizzaro, giving CH3-C(CH2OH)3.

q: Ice at −5°C is heated to become vapour at 110°C at atmospheric pressure. The entropy change is obtained from:
o: ∫(268→273) Cp,m dT + ΔHfus/Tf + ΔHvap/Tb + ∫(273→373) Cp,m dT + ∫(373→383) Cp,m dT
sol: Entropy change sums (Cp/T)dT over each heating stage plus ΔH(transition)/T for melting and vaporisation — exactly option 2 (the others wrongly use Cp dT without dividing by T).

q: The incorrect statement among the following is:
o: PH3 shows lower proton affinity than NH3
SO2 can act as an oxidizing agent but not as a reducing agent
PF3 exists but NF5 does not
sol: In SO2 sulphur is in the intermediate +4 state, so SO2 acts as both an oxidising and a reducing agent. Hence the claim that it cannot reduce is incorrect.

q: 2.8×10⁻³ mol of CO2 is left after removing 10²¹ molecules from an x mg sample. The mass of CO2 taken initially is (NA = 6.02×10²³):

Match List I (name reaction) with List II (product obtainable). List I: (A) Swarts; (B) Sandmeyer; (C) Wurtz-Fittig; (D) Finkelstein. List II: (I) Ethyl benzene; (II) Ethyl iodide; (III) Cyanobenzene; (IV) Ethyl fluoride.
sol: Swarts gives alkyl fluoride (IV); Sandmeyer with CuCN gives cyanobenzene (III); Wurtz-Fittig gives ethylbenzene (I); Finkelstein gives ethyl iodide (II).

q: Heat treatment of muscular pain uses radiation of about 900 nm. Which spectral line of the H atom suits this? (Rydberg constant RH = 10⁵ cm⁻¹)
sol: 1/λ = 1/(9×10⁻⁵ cm) = 1.11×10⁴ cm⁻¹ = RH(1/9), matching the Paschen series limit (∞ → 3).

q: The d-electronic configuration of an octahedral Co(II) complex with magnetic moment 3.95 BM is:
sol: μ = 3.95 BM corresponds to 3 unpaired electrons. Co(II) is d⁷; the high-spin octahedral configuration t2g⁵ eg² has exactly 3 unpaired electrons.

q: The correct stability order of the species p (cyclopropenyl anion), q (cyclopentadienyl anion) and r (cyclooctatetraene ring) is:
sol: Cyclopentadienyl anion (q) has 6 π electrons and is aromatic (most stable). Cyclopropenyl anion (p) has 4 π electrons and is antiaromatic (least stable). Cyclooctatetraene (r) is non-aromatic and lies in between, giving q > r > p.

q: The standard enthalpy and standard entropy of decomposition of N2O4 to NO2 are 55.0 kJ/mol and 175.0 J/K/mol. The standard free energy change at 25°C, in J/mol, is ___ (nearest integer).

For 2 N2O5(g) → 2 N2O4(g) + O2(g) at constant volume, the initial total pressure is 0.6 atm at t=0. With rate constant 4.606×10⁻² s⁻¹ (first order), the total pressure at t = 100 s is x×10⁻³ atm. Find x (nearest integer).
During sulphur estimation, 160 mg of an organic compound gives 466 mg of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur is ___ %. (Ba = 137, S = 32, O = 16)
A 1 mM solution of ethylamine has pH = 9. If its base ionization constant Kb = 10⁻ˣ, find x (nearest integer). (Neglect the degree of ionization compared with unity.)
sol: pH 9 gives [OH⁻] = 10⁻⁵. Kb = [OH⁻]²/C = (10⁻⁵)²/10⁻³ = 10⁻⁷, so x = 7.

q: 4-Nitrotoluene is treated with (i) Br2/Fe, (ii) Sn/HCl, (iii) NaNO2/HCl at 273 K, (iv) H3PO2/H2O to give major product A. The molar mass of A is ___ g/mol. (C=12, H=1, O=16, Br=80, N=14, P=31)
sol: Bromination goes ortho to CH3 (meta to NO2); the nitro group is reduced to amine, diazotised, then removed by H3PO2. Product A is 2-bromotoluene (C7H7Br), molar mass 171.

q: A positive point charge Q is at P on the axis of electric dipole 1 at distance r, and P is also on the equatorial plane of a second dipole 2 at distance r. Both dipoles are made of charges q separated by 2a. For the charge at P to experience no net force, which relation holds?
sol: Balancing the exact axial field of dipole 1 against the exact equatorial field of dipole 2 at P gives a/r of order 3. (Precise geometry is in the figure.)

q: For the given circuit (E = 6 V, a 4 Ω resistor from C to D, a diode from D, and two 4 Ω resistors to B), evaluate: A. Total resistance is 6 Ω. B. Ammeter current is 1 A. C. Potential across AB is 4 V. D. Potential across CD is 4 V. E. Total resistance is 8 Ω. Choose the correct set:
sol: With the diode conducting, the two 4 Ω resistors are in parallel (2 Ω) in series with the 4 Ω, giving 6 Ω (A true). Current = 6/6 = 1 A (B true). The 4 Ω (C–D) drops 1 A × 4 = 4 V (D true). So A, B and D. (Circuit is in the figure.)

q: The distance of the line (x−2)/2 = (y−6)/3 = (z−3)/4 from the point (1,4,0), measured along the line x/1 = (y−2)/2 = (z+3)/3, is:
sol: The line through (1,4,0) with direction (1,2,3) meets the first line at parameter t = 1, i.e. at (2,6,3). Distance = |t|·√(1+4+9) = √14.

q: Let A = {(x,y): |x+y| ≥ 3} and B = {(x,y): |x|+|y| ≤ 3}. If C = {(x,y) ∈ A∩B : x = 0 or y = 0}, then the sum of |x+y| over C is:
sol: On the axes, A and B force the points (0,3), (0,−3), (3,0), (−3,0), each with |x+y| = 3. Sum = 12.

q: Let X = R×R and R be defined by (a1,b1) R (a2,b2) iff b1 = b2. Statement I: R is an equivalence relation. Statement II: For (a,b) ∈ X, S = {(x,y): (x,y) R (a,b)} represents a line parallel to y = x. Choose the correct option:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sol: The relation b1 = b2 is reflexive, symmetric and transitive (I true). But S is the horizontal line y = b, parallel to the x-axis, not to y = x, so Statement II is false.

q: Let ∫ x³ sin x dx = g(x) + C. If 8(g(π/2) + g'(π/2)) = a·π³ + b·π² + c with integers a, b, c, then a + b − c equals:
sol: g(x) = −x³cos x + 3x²sin x + 6x cos x − 6 sin x, g'(x) = x³ sin x. At π/2: 8(3π²/4 − 6 + π³/8) = π³ + 6π² − 48. So a=1, b=6, c=−48 and a+b−c = 55.

q: A rod of length 8 units moves with ends A and B on the lines x−y+2=0 and y+2=0. If the locus of the point P dividing AB internally in ratio 2:1 is 9(x² + a·y² + b·xy + c·x + 28y) − 76 = 0, then a − b − c equals:
sol: With A=(t, t+2), B=(s,−2) and P=(A+2B)/3, eliminating using |AB|=8 gives the locus with a=13, b=−6, c=−4. So a − b − c = 23.

q: If the square of the shortest distance between the lines (x−2)/1 = (y−1)/2 = (z+3)/(−3) and (x+1)/2 = (y+3)/4 = (z+5)/(−5) is m/n (m, n coprime), then m + n equals:
sol: Using |(P2−P1)·(d1×d2)|/|d1×d2|, the squared shortest distance is 4/5, so m + n = 9.

q: Let A divide the segment joining P(−1,−1,2) and Q(5,5,10) internally in the ratio r:1 (r>0). With O the origin, if (OQ · OA) − (1/5)|OP × OA|² = 10, then r equals:
sol: Writing A = (P + rQ)/(1+r) and evaluating the dot and cross products, the equation reduces to r = 7.

q: The length of the chord of the ellipse x²/4 + y²/2 = 1 whose mid-point is (1, 1/2) is:
sol: The chord with mid-point (1, 1/2) is x + y = 3/2 (from T = S1). Its intersection with the ellipse gives length (2/3)√15.

q: The system x+y+z=6, x+2y+5z=9, x+5y+Lz=M has no solution if:
sol: The coefficient determinant is L − 17, which vanishes at L = 17. There the system is inconsistent unless M = 18, so no solution occurs when L = 17 and M ≠ 18.

q: Let the range of f(x) = 6 + 16·cos x·cos(π/3 − x)·cos(π/3 + x)·sin 3x·cos 6x be [α, β]. The distance of the point (α, β) from the line 3x + 4y + 12 = 0 is:
sol: cos x·cos(π/3−x)·cos(π/3+x) = (1/4)cos 3x, so f(x) = 6 + sin 12x with range [5, 7]. Distance of (5,7) from the line = |15+28+12|/5 = 11.

q: Let x = x(y) solve y = (x − y·dx/dy)·sin(x/y), y > 0, with x(1) = π/2. Then cos(x(2)) equals:
sol: With v = x/y the equation gives sin v dv = −dy/y, so cos(x/y) = ln y. At y = 2, cos(x/2) = ln 2, hence cos(x(2)) = 2cos²(x/2) − 1 = 2(ln 2)² − 1.

q: A spherical chocolate ball has a uniform ice-cream layer. When the layer is 1 cm thick, the ice-cream melts at 81 cm³/min and the thickness decreases at 1/(4π) cm/min. The surface area (cm²) of the chocolate ball (without ice-cream) is:
sol: dV/dt = 4π(R+t)²·d(thickness)/dt gives (R+t)² = 81, so R+t = 9. With t = 1, R = 8 and surface area = 4π·64 = 256π.

q: The number of complex numbers z satisfying |z| = 1 and |z/conj(z) + conj(z)/z| = 1 is:
sol: With z = e^(iθ), the expression is |2 cos 2θ| = 1, so cos 2θ = ±1/2. This gives 8 values of θ in [0, 2π).

q: Let A = [aij] be a 3×3 matrix with A·[0,1,0]ᵀ = [0,0,1]ᵀ, A·[4,1,3]ᵀ = [0,1,0]ᵀ and A·[2,1,2]ᵀ = [1,0,0]ᵀ. Then a23 equals:
sol: The first vector gives column 2 of A: a22 = 0. Row 2 then gives 4a21 + 3a23 = 1 and 2a21 + 2a23 = 0, so a21 = −a23 and a23 = −1.

q: If I = ∫₀^(π/2) sin^(3/2)x / (sin^(3/2)x + cos^(3/2)x) dx, then ∫₀^(2I) (x·sin x·cos x)/(sin⁴x + cos⁴x) dx equals:
sol: By the King's-property, I = π/4, so the upper limit is 2I = π/2. Evaluating the second integral over [0, π/2] gives π²/16.

q: A 4×4 board has 16 unit squares. Two squares are chosen at random. The probability that they have no side in common is:
sol: Total pairs = C(16,2) = 120; side-sharing pairs = 12 + 12 = 24. P(no common side) = 1 − 24/120 = 4/5.

q: Let the shortest distance from (a,0), a>0, to the parabola y² = 4x be 4. The equation of the circle through (a,0) and the focus, with centre on the axis of the parabola, is:
sol: Shortest distance 2√(a−1) = 4 gives a = 5. The circle through (5,0) and focus (1,0) with centre on the x-axis has centre (3,0), radius 2: x²+y²−6x+5=0.

q: If in the expansion of (1+x)^p·(1−x)^q the coefficients of x and x² are 1 and −2 respectively, then p² + q² equals:
sol: Coefficient of x: p − q = 1. Coefficient of x²: (p−q)² − (p+q) = −2 gives p + q = 5. So p = 3, q = 2 and p² + q² = 13.

q: If the area of the region {(x,y): −1 ≤ x ≤ 1, 0 ≤ y ≤ a + e^|x| − e^(−x), a > 0} is (e² + 8e + 1)/e, then a equals:
sol: Area = 2a + e − 2 + 1/e. Setting this equal to e + 8 + 1/e gives 2a − 2 = 8, so a = 5.

q: The variance of the numbers 8, 21, 34, 47, …, 320 is ___
sol: These 25 terms form an AP (first term 8, common difference 13). Its variance is 8788.

q: The roots of 3x² − px + q = 0 are the 10th and 11th terms of an AP with common difference 3/2. If the sum of the first 11 terms is 88, then q − 2p equals ___
sol: Sum of 11 terms = 11(a + 5d) = 88 gives a = 1/2. The 10th and 11th terms are 14 and 15.5, so p = 3·29.5 = 88.5, q = 3·217 = 651, and q − 2p = 474.

q: The number of ways 5 boys and 4 girls can sit in a row so that either all the boys sit together or no two boys sit together is ___
sol: All boys together: 5!·5! = 14400. No two boys together: 4!·5! = 2880. These are disjoint, so total = 17280.

q: The focus of the parabola y² = 4x + 16 is the centre of a circle C of radius 5. If the values of L for which C passes through the intersection of 3x − y = 0 and x + Ly = 4 are L1 and L2 (L1 < L2), then 12·L1 + 29·L2 equals ___
sol: Focus is (−3,0); circle (x+3)² + y² = 25. The intersection point (4/(1+3L), 12/(1+3L)) on the circle gives L = −7/6 and 1. So 12(−7/6) + 29(1) = −14 + 29 = 15.

q: Let α, β be roots of x² − a·x − b = 0 with Im(α) < Im(β), and Pn = αⁿ − βⁿ. If P3 = −5√7·i, P4 = −3√7·i, P5 = 11√7·i and P6 = 45√7·i, then |α⁴ + β⁴| equals ___
sol: The recurrence Pn = a·P(n−1) + b·P(n−2) gives a = 3, b = −4, so x² − 3x + 4 = 0. Then α²+β² = 1 and α⁴+β⁴ = 1 − 32 = −31, so |α⁴+β⁴| = 31.

q: A galvanometer of coil resistance 30 Ω needs 20 mA for full-scale deflection. To measure a maximum current of 3 A, a shunt of 30/X Ω is added. The value of X is:
A ball with kinetic energy KE is projected at 60° to the horizontal. The kinetic energy at the highest point of its flight is:
sol: At the top only the horizontal component v·cos60° = v/2 remains, so KE_top = ½m(v/2)² = KE/4.

q: Two charges 7 μC and −4 μC are placed at (−7 cm, 0, 0) and (7 cm, 0, 0). The electrostatic potential energy of the configuration is (ε0 = 8.85×10⁻¹²):
Two charges −4 μC and 4 μC form a dipole at (−9,0,0) cm and (9,0,0) cm in a uniform field of 10⁴ N/C. The work done to rotate the dipole from equilibrium through 180° is:
A massless spring elongates by x1 under 5 N and by x2 under 7 N. For an elongation of (5·x1 − 2·x2), the tension in the spring is:
Water of mass m grams is slowly heated from T1 to T2. The change in entropy (specific heat = 1 J/kg/K) is:
sol: dS = ∫ m·c·dT/T = m·c·ln(T2/T1) = m·ln(T2/T1) with c = 1.

q: Water flows in a horizontal pipe with one end closed by a valve. The pressure gauge reads P1; on opening the valve it falls to P2. The speed of the flowing water is proportional to:
sol: By Bernoulli, P1 − P2 = ½ρv², so v ∝ √(P1 − P2).

q: A concave mirror of focal length f in air is dipped in a liquid of refractive index μ. Its focal length in the liquid becomes:
sol: A mirror's focal length depends only on its radius of curvature (f = R/2) and is independent of the surrounding medium, so it stays f.

q: In the circuit shown (a 5 V source with two parallel branches, each a diode in series with a 20 Ω resistor), the current through the battery is:
sol: With both diodes forward biased, the two 20 Ω resistors are in parallel (10 Ω), so current = 5/10 = 0.5 A. (Diode orientations are in the figure.)

q: The refractive index of a glass prism is √3, and the angle of minimum deviation equals the angle of the prism. The angle of the prism is:
sol: With δm = A, μ = sin A/sin(A/2) = 2cos(A/2). So 2cos(A/2) = √3 gives A/2 = 30°, A = 60°.

q: In Young's double slit experiment, one slit has width d and the other x·d. If the ratio of maximum to minimum intensity is 9:4, then x is (field strength proportional to slit width):
sol: Amplitude ∝ width, so √(Imax/Imin) = 3/2 = (1+x)/(x−1) for x>1, giving x = 5.

q: For the P-V path A(2V0,P0) → B(3V0,P0) → C(3V0,2P0) → D(V0,2P0), the work done by the ideal gas along ABCD is:
img: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 300 210'><line x1='50' y1='180' x2='285' y2='180' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='285,180 277,176 277,184' fill='#0f172a'/><line x1='50' y1='190' x2='50' y2='30' stroke='#0f172a' stroke-width='1.5'/><polygon points='50,30 46,38 54,38' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='40' y='28' font-size='11'>P</text><text x='278' y='196' font-size='11'>V</text><line x1='180' y1='120' x2='250' y2='120' stroke='#b91c1c' stroke-width='2'/><polygon points='250,120 242,116 242,124' fill='#b91c1c'/><line x1='250' y1='120' x2='250' y2='60' stroke='#b91c1c' stroke-width='2'/><polygon points='250,60 246,68 254,68' fill='#b91c1c'/><line x1='250' y1='60' x2='110' y2='60' stroke='#b91c1c' stroke-width='2'/><polygon points='110,60 118,56 118,64' fill='#b91c1c'/><circle cx='180' cy='120' r='2.5' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='176' y='134' font-size='11'>A</text><circle cx='250' cy='120' r='2.5' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='254' y='134' font-size='11'>B</text><circle cx='250' cy='60' r='2.5' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='254' y='56' font-size='11'>C</text><circle cx='110' cy='60' r='2.5' fill='#0f172a'/><text x='100' y='56' font-size='11'>D</text><text x='16' y='124' font-size='9'>P0</text><text x='12' y='64' font-size='9'>2P0</text><text x='102' y='196' font-size='9'>V0</text><text x='168' y='196' font-size='9'>2V0</text><text x='240' y='196' font-size='9'>3V0</text></svg>
sol: A→B (isobaric): +P0·V0. B→C (isochoric): 0. C→D (isobaric): 2P0·(V0−3V0) = −4P0V0. Total = −3 P0V0.

q: A plane EM wave of frequency 20 MHz travels along +x. At a point the electric field is Ey = 9.3 V/m. The magnetic field there is:
sol: B = E/c = 9.3/3×10⁸ = 3.1×10⁻⁸ T, directed along +z since propagation is +x and E is +y.

q: A transverse wave on a string is y(x,t) = 4.0·sin[20×10⁻³·x + 600t] mm (x in mm, t in s). The wave velocity is:
sol: v = ω/k = 600/(20×10⁻³) = 3×10⁴ mm/s = 30 m/s, and the (kx + ωt) form means motion along −x, so −30 m/s.

q: Assertion (A): The binding energy per nucleon is nearly independent of A for nuclei with mass numbers 30–170. Reason (R): The nuclear force is long range. Choose the correct option:
o: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
sol: The binding energy per nucleon is roughly constant in that range (A true), but the nuclear force is short range, so R is false.

q: A satellite orbits the Earth 9 times closer than the Moon. If the Moon's period is 27 days, the satellite's period of rotation is:
sol: By Kepler's third law, T ∝ r^(3/2). T_sat = 27·(1/9)^(3/2) = 27/27 = 1 day.

q: A disc of radius R and mass M rotates about an axis perpendicular to it. An external torque makes θ(t) = 5t² − 8t. The power delivered by the torque at t = 2 s is:
sol: α = 10, torque = I·α = ½MR²·10 = 5MR²; ω(2) = 10·2−8 = 12. Power = 5MR²·12 = 60 MR².

q: The energy of a system is E(t) = a³·e^(−b·t) with b = 0.3 s⁻¹. If errors in a and t are 1.2% and 1.6%, the maximum percentage error in E at t = 5 s is:

Match List I with List II. List I: (A) Permeability of free space; (B) Magnetic field; (C) Magnetic moment; (D) Torsional constant. List II: (I) [M L² T⁻²]; (II) [M T⁻² A⁻¹]; (III) [M L T⁻² A⁻²]; (IV) [L² A].
sol: μ0 = [M L T⁻² A⁻²] (III); B = [M T⁻² A⁻¹] (II); magnetic moment = [L² A] (IV); torsional constant = [M L² T⁻²] (I).

q: In the photoelectric effect, the work function is 2.14 eV and the stopping potential is 2 V. The wavelength of the incident EM wave is (hc = 1242 eV·nm):
sol: E = KE_max + work function = 2 + 2.14 = 4.14 eV. λ = 1242/4.14 = 300 nm.

q: A time-varying potential difference is applied to a parallel plate capacitor of 2.5 μF (dielectric constant 1). If the displacement current is 0.25 mA, the magnitude of the rate of change of potential difference is ___ V/s.
A series LCR circuit has R = 300 Ω, C = 25 nF and L = 100 mH. For maximum current, the angular frequency of the source is ___ ×10⁴ rad/s.

An air bubble of radius 1.0 mm is at a depth of 20 cm below the surface of a liquid of surface tension 0.095 J/m² and density 10³ kg/m³. The difference between the pressure inside the bubble and atmospheric pressure is ___ N/m². (g = 10 m/s²)

A satellite of mass M/2 orbits the Earth in a circular orbit at height R/3 from the surface. Its angular momentum is M·√(GMR/x). Find x. (M and R are Earth's mass and radius, G the gravitational constant)
sol: Orbital radius r = 4R/3, v = √(GM/r). L = (M/2)·v·r = M·√(GMR/3), so x = 3.

q: In the circuit shown (8 μF capacitor, 10 Ω and 15 Ω resistors, 5 V source), the steady-state charge on the capacitor is ___ μC.
sol: In steady state, current = 5/(10+15) = 0.2 A. The capacitor is across the 10 Ω resistor, so V = 0.2·10 = 2 V and Q = 8·2 = 16 μC. (Exact topology is in the figure.)

q: Chlorobenzene is treated with (i) NaOH at 623 K and 300 atm, (ii) H⁺ to give [A], which on treatment with Na2Cr2O7/H2SO4 gives [B]. Identify [A] and [B]:
sol: The Dow process converts chlorobenzene to phenol (A). Oxidation of phenol with acidified dichromate gives 1,4-benzoquinone (B).

q: In the sequence K2Cr2O7 →(KOH, −H2O) [A] →(H2SO4, −H2O) [B] + K2SO4, the products [A] and [B] respectively are:
sol: In base, dichromate converts to chromate: [A] = K2CrO4. In acid, the chromate reverts to dichromate: [B] = K2Cr2O7.

q: Regarding the effect of temperature on spontaneity, consider: (A) ΔH>0, ΔS<0 → non-spontaneous at any T; (B) ΔH>0, ΔS>0 → spontaneous at low T; (C) ΔH<0, ΔS<0 → non-spontaneous at low T; (D) ΔH<0, ΔS>0 → spontaneous at any T. Which rows are INCORRECTLY represented?
sol: By ΔG = ΔH − TΔS: (A) is always positive → non-spontaneous (correct); (D) is always negative → spontaneous (correct). (B) is spontaneous at HIGH T, not low; (C) is spontaneous at low T. So (B) and (C) are the incorrectly represented rows.

q: Which description most appropriately represents a zero-order reaction?
o: Reactant concentration decreases linearly with time
Reactant concentration stays constant with time
sol: For a zero-order reaction the rate is constant while the reactant concentration decreases linearly with time (a straight declining line).

q: For X2Y(g) ⇌ X2(g) + ½Y2(g), the relation between the degree of dissociation x (very small) of X2Y and Kp is:
sol: For small x, Kp = x·√(x·p/2) = x^(3/2)·√(p/2). Solving gives x = ∛(2Kp²/p).

q: For the hydration equilibrium R2C=O + H2O ⇌ R2C(OH)2: Statement I: For formaldehyde K ≈ 2280 because small substituents make hydration favourable. Statement II: For trichloroacetaldehyde K ≈ 2000 due to the −I effect of −Cl. Choose the correct option:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
sol: Formaldehyde hydrates readily (small H substituents, high K), and the electron-withdrawing −I effect of Cl in trichloroacetaldehyde also favours hydration. Both statements are true.

q: Statement I: For a given shell the total number of allowed orbitals is n². Statement II: For any subshell, the spatial orientations of the orbitals are given by −l to +l including zero. Choose the correct option:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sol: A shell with principal number n has n² orbitals (I true), and each subshell has orientations from −l to +l including 0, giving 2l+1 orbitals (II true).

q: Given E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = 0.34 V, E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, E°(Ag⁺/Ag) = 0.80 V, E°(Mg²⁺/Mg) = −2.37 V, which cell gives the most negative value of ΔG?
sol: Most negative ΔG means most positive E_cell. Zn–Ag gives E_cell = 0.80 − (−0.76) = 1.56 V, the largest positive value.

q: The α-helix and β-pleated sheet structures of a protein are associated with its:
sol: α-helix and β-pleated sheet arrangements define the secondary structure of proteins.

q: Given the atomic numbers of some group-14 elements, the element with the lowest melting point is (atomic number):
sol: Among C, Si, Ge, Sn, Pb, tin (Z = 50) has the lowest melting point (about 232 °C, lower even than lead).

q: Statement I: A plot of √ν (ν = frequency of characteristic X-rays) vs atomic mass is a straight line. Statement II: A plot of ν vs atomic number is a straight line. Choose the correct option:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sol: Moseley's law gives √ν linear with atomic NUMBER, not atomic mass (I false), and ν itself is not linear with atomic number (II false). Both are false.

q: Identify A, B and C: A →(HNO3) Pb(NO3)2 →(H2SO4) B →(ammonium acetate/acetic acid/K2CrO4) C.
sol: PbS dissolves in HNO3 to give Pb(NO3)2 (A = PbS); with H2SO4 it forms white PbSO4 (B); with acetate buffer and chromate it gives yellow PbCrO4 (C).

q: Statement I: The boiling points of alcohols and phenols increase with increasing number of carbon atoms. Statement II: The boiling points of alcohols and phenols are higher than those of comparable ethers and haloalkanes. Choose the correct option:
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
sol: Boiling point rises with molecular size (I true), and hydrogen bonding makes alcohols/phenols boil higher than comparable ethers or haloalkanes (II true).

q: For a binary solution of two volatile liquids 1 and 2, with x1 and y1 the mole fractions of component 1 in liquid and vapour, the slope and intercept of the linear plot of 1/x1 vs 1/y1 are respectively:
sol: From Raoult's law, 1/x1 = (P1*/P2*)(1/y1) + (P2*−P1*)/P2*, giving slope P1*/P2* and intercept (P2*−P1*)/P2*.

q: Arrange the four bromides shown (A, B, C, D) in ascending order of their relative rate of solvolysis (SN1):
sol: SN1 solvolysis rate follows carbocation stability. The benzhydryl bromide (C) forms the most stabilized (dibenzylic) cation and reacts fastest, giving (D) < (A) < (B) < (C). (Structures are in the figure.)

q: Match List I (alloy) with List II (composition). List I: (A) Bronze; (B) Brass; (C) UK silver coin (cupronickel); (D) Stainless steel. List II: (I) Cu, Ni; (II) Fe, Cr, Ni, C; (III) Cu, Zn; (IV) Cu, Sn.
sol: Bronze = Cu,Sn (IV); Brass = Cu,Zn (III); UK silver coin (cupronickel) = Cu,Ni (I); Stainless steel = Fe,Cr,Ni,C (II).

q: Match List I (isomers of C10H14) with List II (their ozonolysis products), as shown in the figure.
sol: Matching each C10H14 isomer to the dicarbonyl fragments produced on ozonolysis gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II. (Structures are in the figure.)

q: The pH of water is 7 at 25 °C. If water is heated to 80 °C, its pH will:
o: H⁺ concentration increases while OH⁻ concentration decreases
sol: Heating increases Kw, so both [H⁺] and [OH⁻] rise equally (water stays neutral) and the pH decreases.

q: Identify the coordination complexes in which the central metal ion has a d⁴ configuration: (A) [FeO4]²⁻, (B) [Mn(CN)6]³⁻, (C) [Fe(CN)6]³⁻, (D) Cr2(O2CMe)4(H2O)2, (E) [NiF6]²⁻.
sol: Mn(III) in [Mn(CN)6]³⁻ is d⁴, and Cr(II) in the acetate is d⁴. [FeO4]²⁻ is Fe(VI) d², [Fe(CN)6]³⁻ is d⁵, [NiF6]²⁻ is Ni(IV) d⁶. So only B and D.

q: Adding a non-volatile solute lowers the solvent's vapour pressure by 10 mm Hg when the solute mole fraction is 0.2. If instead the lowering is 20 mm Hg, the mole fraction of the solvent is:
sol: ΔP = P0·x_solute, so P0 = 10/0.2 = 50. For 20 mm Hg lowering, x_solute = 20/50 = 0.4, hence x_solvent = 0.6.

q: 0.01 mole of an organic compound X containing 10% hydrogen by mass, on complete combustion, produces 0.9 g of H2O. The molar mass of X is ___ g/mol.
sol: 0.9 g H2O = 0.05 mol → 0.1 mol H, i.e. 10 H atoms per molecule = 10 g/mol of H = 10% of M, so M = 100 g/mol.

q: A compound X′ absorbs 2 moles of H2, and on oxidation with KMnO4/H⁺ gives CH3-CO-CH3, CH3-COOH and CH3-CO-CH2CH2-COOH. The total number of sigma bonds present in X′ is ___
sol: The fragments imply X′ = (CH3)2C=C(CH3)-CH2-CH2-CH=CH-CH3 (C10H18). It has 18 C–H sigma bonds and 9 C–C sigma bonds, giving 27 sigma bonds in total.

q: When 81.0 g of aluminium reacts with 128.0 g of oxygen gas, the mass of aluminium oxide produced is ___ g (nearest integer). (Al = 27, O = 16)
sol: 4Al + 3O2 → 2Al2O3. 3 mol Al needs 2.25 mol O2 (4 mol available), so Al is limiting. Al2O3 = 1.5 mol × 102 = 153 g.

q: Using a Born-Haber cycle with ΔH(lattice) = 800, ΔH(sublimation) = 100, ΔH(ionization) = 500, ΔH(electron gain) = −300 and ΔHf(M⁺X⁻) = −400 kJ/mol, the bond dissociation enthalpy of X2 is ___ kJ/mol (nearest integer).
sol: ΔHf = sublimation + IE + ½·Bond + EGE − lattice: −400 = 100 + 500 + ½·Bond − 300 − 800, giving ½·Bond = 100, so Bond = 200 kJ/mol.

q: 4-Ethoxyaniline is diazotised (NaNO2/HCl, 0–5 °C), coupled with phenol/NaOH then acidified to give the azo dye B (C14H14N2O2). B is then treated with (i) NaOH (ii) ethyl bromide to give major product C (C16H18N2O2). The total number of sp³ hybridised carbon atoms in C is ___
sol: Product C is the bis-ethoxy azo compound (EtO-C6H4-N=N-C6H4-OEt). Only the two ethyl groups are sp³, contributing 2 carbons each, for a total of 4 sp³ carbons.
